verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: मय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ विश्वपोत इतस्ततः । भ्रमति स्वान्तवातेन न ममास्त्यसहिष्णुता ॥
verses.iast: mayyanantamahāmbhodhau viśvapota itastataḥ | bhramati svāntavātena na mamāstyasahiṣṇutā ||
verses.en: In me, the endless ocean, the ship of the world drifts here and there, driven by its own wind. I am not troubled by it.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 7.1 is a verse from chapter 7 (The ship on the ocean). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "In me, the endless ocean, the ship of the world drifts here and there, driven by its own wind. I am not troubled by it."
verses.notice: The ship of the world is moved by its own wind, and the ocean does not mind.

words.m: by the wind of its own mind

verses.commentary: In chapter 2 the ship of the world sank when the wind of the mind fell still. Here, in chapter 7, Janaka watches the ship drift here and there, pushed by its own wind, and says he feels no impatience about it. Asahiṣṇutā is the inability to bear something. Its absence is a calm tolerance, the kind a deep sea has toward the boats on its surface. The phrase svāntavātena can be read as by its own inner wind, the mind of each being. The world moves according to the minds within it. The ocean does not steer the ship. The Advaita reading draws a practical lesson. Much of our distress comes from wanting the world to move differently, and from feeling that it is our job to steer all of it. The knower still acts where action is his to take, and is not tormented by the drifting of everything else. Chapter 7 has five verses in this voice, each one Janaka settling more fully into the view his teacher gave him.

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: मय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ जगद्वीचिः स्वभावतः । उदेतु वास्तमायातु न मे वृद्धिर्न च क्षतिः ॥
verses.iast: mayyanantamahāmbhodhau jagadvīciḥ svabhāvataḥ | udetu vāstamāyātu na me vṛddhirna ca kṣatiḥ ||
verses.en: In me, the endless ocean, the wave of the world rises or sinks by its own nature. I neither grow nor shrink.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 7.2 is a verse from chapter 7 (The ship on the ocean). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "In me, the endless ocean, the wave of the world rises or sinks by its own nature. I neither grow nor shrink."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: मय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ विश्वं नाम विकल्पना । अतिशान्तो निराकार एतदेवाहमास्थितः ॥
verses.iast: mayyanantamahāmbhodhau viśvaṃ nāma vikalpanā | atiśānto nirākāra etadevāhamāsthitaḥ ||
verses.en: In me, the endless ocean, the world is only imagined. I am at complete peace and without form. In this alone I rest.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 7.3 is a verse from chapter 7 (The ship on the ocean). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "In me, the endless ocean, the world is only imagined. I am at complete peace and without form. In this alone I rest."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: नात्मा भावेषु नो भावस्तत्रानन्ते निरञ्जने । इत्यसक्तोऽस्पृहः शान्त एतदेवाहमास्थितः ॥
verses.iast: nātmā bhāveṣu no bhāvastatrānante nirañjane | ityasakto'spṛhaḥ śānta etadevāhamāsthitaḥ ||
verses.en: The Self is not in objects, and no object is in the Self, which is endless and spotless. So I am unattached, without craving, at peace. In this alone I rest.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 7.4 is a verse from chapter 7 (The ship on the ocean). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "The Self is not in objects, and no object is in the Self, which is endless and spotless. So I am unattached, without craving, at peace. In this alone I rest."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: अहो चिन्मात्रमेवाहमिन्द्रजालोपमं जगत् । इति मम कथं कुत्र हेयोपादेयकल्पना ॥
verses.iast: aho cinmātramevāhamindrajālopamaṃ jagat | iti mama kathaṃ kutra heyopādeyakalpanā ||
verses.en: How strange. I am awareness alone, and the world is like a magic show. So how, and where, could I imagine anything to reject or accept?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 7.5 is a verse from chapter 7 (The ship on the ocean). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "How strange. I am awareness alone, and the world is like a magic show. So how, and where, could I imagine anything to reject or accept?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: तदा बन्धो यदा चित्तं किञ्चिद् वाञ्छति शोचति । किञ्चिन् मुञ्चति गृण्हाति किञ्चिद् दृष्यति कुप्यति ॥
verses.iast: tadā bandho yadā cittaṃ kiñcid vāñchati śocati | kiñcin muñcati gṛṇhāti kiñcid dṛṣyati kupyati ||
verses.en: It is bondage when the mind wants something or grieves over something, lets go of something or grabs something, is pleased by something or angry at something.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 8.1 is a verse from chapter 8 (Bondage and freedom). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "It is bondage when the mind wants something or grieves over something, lets go of something or grabs something, is pleased by something or angry at something."
verses.notice: Six movements of the mind are listed, and each one is called bondage.
verses.commentary: Chapter 8 is four verses long and gives the clearest definition of bondage and freedom in the text. This first verse lists six movements: wanting, grieving, letting go, grabbing, delight and anger. The word kiñcit, something, repeats through the line. Bondage happens when the mind does any of these about something. Notice that letting go is on the list. Even renouncing something, if the mind grips the act of renouncing, is bondage. The Advaita commentators read the verse as a description of where bondage lives. Objects are neutral and the Self is free, so bondage can only live in the mind's reaching and recoiling. That makes the verse usable. The next time you feel pulled by a want or a grievance, you can name it: this is the movement Ashtavakra called bondage. Naming it will not end it. It does show you where it lives. The following verse gives the mirror image, the same six movements absent, and calls that freedom.

bridge.note: Krishna traces how dwelling on objects breeds attachment, then desire, then anger.

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: तदा मुक्तिर्यदा चित्तं न वाञ्छति न शोचति । न मुञ्चति न गृण्हाति न हृष्यति न कुप्यति ॥
verses.iast: tadā muktiryadā cittaṃ na vāñchati na śocati | na muñcati na gṛṇhāti na hṛṣyati na kupyati ||
verses.en: It is freedom when the mind does not want and does not grieve, does not let go and does not grab, is not pleased and is not angry.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 8.2 is a verse from chapter 8 (Bondage and freedom). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "It is freedom when the mind does not want and does not grieve, does not let go and does not grab, is not pleased and is not angry."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: तदा बन्धो यदा चित्तं सक्तं काश्वपि दृष्टिषु । तदा मोक्षो यदा चित्तमसक्तं सर्वदृष्टिषु ॥
verses.iast: tadā bandho yadā cittaṃ saktaṃ kāśvapi dṛṣṭiṣu | tadā mokṣo yadā cittamasaktaṃ sarvadṛṣṭiṣu ||
verses.en: It is bondage when the mind is attached to any one experience. It is freedom when the mind is attached to none.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 8.3 is a verse from chapter 8 (Bondage and freedom). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "It is bondage when the mind is attached to any one experience. It is freedom when the mind is attached to none."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: यदा नाहं तदा मोक्षो यदाहं बन्धनं तदा । मत्वेति हेलया किञ्चिन्मा गृहाण विमुञ्च मा ॥
verses.iast: yadā nāhaṃ tadā mokṣo yadāhaṃ bandhanaṃ tadā | matveti helayā kiñcinmā gṛhāṇa vimuñca mā ||
verses.en: When there is no 'I', there is freedom. When there is 'I', there is bondage. Knowing this, lightly, take nothing and drop nothing.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 8.4 is a verse from chapter 8 (Bondage and freedom). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "When there is no 'I', there is freedom. When there is 'I', there is bondage. Knowing this, lightly, take nothing and drop nothing."
verses.notice: The word helayā, lightly or playfully, sets the tone for the whole instruction.
verses.commentary: The first line is as short as Sanskrit allows. When there is no I, there is freedom. When there is I, there is bondage. Aham here means the ego-sense, the small self that claims things, and not the Self of the earlier chapters. Then comes the instruction, and its most important word is helayā. It means lightly, easily, as if in play. Having seen this, says Ashtavakra, do not grab anything and do not drop anything, and do it lightly. The tradition reads helayā as a guard against turning the teaching into another strain. If you fight the ego with the ego, you have doubled it. If you try hard to neither grasp nor reject, you are grasping at non-grasping. The light touch is the method. It resembles holding a bird: too tight and you hurt it, too loose and it goes. With this verse the four-verse chapter ends, having said in four verses what some texts take volumes to say.

bridge.note: Krishna says peace comes to one who lives without craving, without 'mine' and without 'I'.

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: कृताकृते च द्वन्द्वानि कदा शान्तानि कस्य वा । एवं ज्ञात्वेह निर्वेदाद् भव त्यागपरोऽव्रती ॥
verses.iast: kṛtākṛte ca dvandvāni kadā śāntāni kasya vā | evaṃ jñātveha nirvedād bhava tyāgaparo'vratī ||
verses.en: Things done and things left undone, the pairs of opposites: when have they ever ended, and for whom? Knowing this, grow weary of it all, let go, and keep no vows.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 9.1 is a verse from chapter 9 (Weariness with the world). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Things done and things left undone, the pairs of opposites: when have they ever ended, and for whom? Knowing this, grow weary of it all, let go, and keep no vows."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: कस्यापि तात धन्यस्य लोकचेष्टावलोकनात् । जीवितेच्छा बुभुक्षा च बुभुत्सोपशमः गताः ॥
verses.iast: kasyāpi tāta dhanyasya lokaceṣṭāvalokanāt | jīvitecchā bubhukṣā ca bubhutsopaśamaḥ gatāḥ ||
verses.en: My child, rare is the fortunate one whose wish to live, to enjoy and to know has been put out by watching how people live.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 9.2 is a verse from chapter 9 (Weariness with the world). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "My child, rare is the fortunate one whose wish to live, to enjoy and to know has been put out by watching how people live."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: अनित्यं सर्वमेवेदं तापत्रितयदूषितम् । असारं निन्दितं हेयमिति निश्चित्य शाम्यति ॥
verses.iast: anityaṃ sarvamevedaṃ tāpatritayadūṣitam | asāraṃ ninditaṃ heyamiti niścitya śāmyati ||
verses.en: All this passes. It is spoiled by the three kinds of suffering, empty, worth little, fit to be left. Certain of this, one becomes still.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 9.3 is a verse from chapter 9 (Weariness with the world). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "All this passes. It is spoiled by the three kinds of suffering, empty, worth little, fit to be left. Certain of this, one becomes still."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: कोऽसौ कालो वयः किं वा यत्र द्वन्द्वानि नो नृणाम् । तान्युपेक्ष्य यथाप्राप्तवर्ती सिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् ॥
verses.iast: ko'sau kālo vayaḥ kiṃ vā yatra dvandvāni no nṛṇām | tānyupekṣya yathāprāptavartī siddhimavāpnuyāt ||
verses.en: What time, what age of life is free of the pairs of opposites for anyone? Ignore them, live with what comes, and you reach the goal.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 9.4 is a verse from chapter 9 (Weariness with the world). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "What time, what age of life is free of the pairs of opposites for anyone? Ignore them, live with what comes, and you reach the goal."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: नाना मतं महर्षीणां साधूनां योगिनां तथा । दृष्ट्वा निर्वेदमापन्नः को न शाम्यति मानवः ॥
verses.iast: nānā mataṃ maharṣīṇāṃ sādhūnāṃ yogināṃ tathā | dṛṣṭvā nirvedamāpannaḥ ko na śāmyati mānavaḥ ||
verses.en: Seeing how great sages, saints and yogis differ in their views, who would not grow weary of it all and fall quiet?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 9.5 is a verse from chapter 9 (Weariness with the world). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Seeing how great sages, saints and yogis differ in their views, who would not grow weary of it all and fall quiet?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: कृत्वा मूर्तिपरिज्ञानं चैतन्यस्य न किं गुरुः । निर्वेदसमतायुक्त्या यस्तारयति संसृतेः ॥
verses.iast: kṛtvā mūrtiparijñānaṃ caitanyasya na kiṃ guruḥ | nirvedasamatāyuktyā yastārayati saṃsṛteḥ ||
verses.en: One who comes to know the nature of awareness through weariness with the world, evenness of mind and reasoning, and so crosses the round of birth and death: is he not a guru?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 9.6 is a verse from chapter 9 (Weariness with the world). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "One who comes to know the nature of awareness through weariness with the world, evenness of mind and reasoning, and so crosses the round of birth and death: is he not a guru?"
verses.notice: The verse asks a question and expects the answer yes: such a person is a guru.

words.m: from the round of birth and death

verses.commentary: Chapter 9 is often titled nirveda, weariness with the world, and this verse explains how that weariness can become freedom. Three means are named: nirveda itself, samatā or evenness of mind, and yukti, reasoning. Through them a person comes to know the nature of awareness, mūrti meaning its true form. Such a person tārayati, carries across the river of saṃsāra. The verb can mean crossing oneself or ferrying others, and the commentators allow both. Then the question: is such a person not a guru? The verse widens the idea of a teacher. A guru here is defined by what they have understood and by their ability to cross. Title and lineage are not mentioned. This fits the story of the text, in which a boy with a bent body teaches a king. People searching 'Ashtavakra Gita 9.6' sometimes land on Bhagavad Gita 9.6, which is a different verse about all beings resting in God as the wind rests in space. The two texts agree on the role of the teacher.

bridge.note: Krishna says the wise who have seen the truth will teach you, if you approach them with humility and questions.

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: पश्य भूतविकारांस्त्वं भूतमात्रान् यथार्थतः । तत्क्षणाद् बन्धनिर्मुक्तः स्वरूपस्थो भविष्यसि ॥
verses.iast: paśya bhūtavikārāṃstvaṃ bhūtamātrān yathārthataḥ | tatkṣaṇād bandhanirmuktaḥ svarūpastho bhaviṣyasi ||
verses.en: See the changes of the elements as only the elements, as they are. That very moment you will be free of bondage and stand in your own nature.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 9.7 is a verse from chapter 9 (Weariness with the world). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "See the changes of the elements as only the elements, as they are. That very moment you will be free of bondage and stand in your own nature."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: वासना एव संसार इति सर्वा विमुञ्च ताः । तत्त्यागो वासनात्यागात्स्थितिरद्य यथा तथा ॥
verses.iast: vāsanā eva saṃsāra iti sarvā vimuñca tāḥ | tattyāgo vāsanātyāgātsthitiradya yathā tathā ||
verses.en: Habit-tendencies are the world. So let all of them go. Dropping them is dropping the world. Then stay as you are, as things come.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 9.8 is a verse from chapter 9 (Weariness with the world). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Habit-tendencies are the world. So let all of them go. Dropping them is dropping the world. Then stay as you are, as things come."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: विहाय वैरिणं काममर्थं चानर्थसङ्कुलम् । धर्ममप्येतयोर्हेतुं सर्वत्रानादरं कुरु ॥
verses.iast: vihāya vairiṇaṃ kāmamarthaṃ cānarthasaṅkulam | dharmamapyetayorhetuṃ sarvatrānādaraṃ kuru ||
verses.en: Leave desire, which is your enemy, and wealth, which comes tangled with harm, and even dharma, which is the cause of both. Be indifferent to all of it.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 10.1 is a verse from chapter 10 (Quiet). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Leave desire, which is your enemy, and wealth, which comes tangled with harm, and even dharma, which is the cause of both. Be indifferent to all of it."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: स्वप्नेन्द्रजालवत् पश्य दिनानि त्रीणि पञ्च वा । मित्रक्षेत्रधनागारदारदायादिसम्पदः ॥
verses.iast: svapnendrajālavat paśya dināni trīṇi pañca vā | mitrakṣetradhanāgāradāradāyādisampadaḥ ||
verses.en: Look on friends, land, money, houses, wife, gifts and other good fortune as a dream or a magic show lasting three or five days.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 10.2 is a verse from chapter 10 (Quiet). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Look on friends, land, money, houses, wife, gifts and other good fortune as a dream or a magic show lasting three or five days."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: यत्र यत्र भवेत्तृष्णा संसारं विद्धि तत्र वै । प्रौढवैराग्यमाश्रित्य वीततृष्णः सुखी भव ॥
verses.iast: yatra yatra bhavettṛṣṇā saṃsāraṃ viddhi tatra vai | prauḍhavairāgyamāśritya vītatṛṣṇaḥ sukhī bhava ||
verses.en: Wherever craving arises, know that the world is there. Take up mature dispassion, let craving go, and be happy.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 10.3 is a verse from chapter 10 (Quiet). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Wherever craving arises, know that the world is there. Take up mature dispassion, let craving go, and be happy."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: तृष्णामात्रात्मको बन्धस्तन्नाशो मोक्ष उच्यते । भवासंसक्तिमात्रेण प्राप्तितुष्टिर्मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
verses.iast: tṛṣṇāmātrātmako bandhastannāśo mokṣa ucyate | bhavāsaṃsaktimātreṇa prāptituṣṭirmuhurmuhuḥ ||
verses.en: Bondage is nothing but craving. Its end is called freedom. Simply by not clinging to the world, you find contentment again and again.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 10.4 is a verse from chapter 10 (Quiet). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Bondage is nothing but craving. Its end is called freedom. Simply by not clinging to the world, you find contentment again and again."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: त्वमेकश्चेतनः शुद्धो जडं विश्वमसत्तथा । अविद्यापि न किञ्चित्सा का बुभुत्सा तथापि ते ॥
verses.iast: tvamekaścetanaḥ śuddho jaḍaṃ viśvamasattathā | avidyāpi na kiñcitsā kā bubhutsā tathāpi te ||
verses.en: You are one, aware and pure. The world is inert and unreal. Not knowing is nothing either. So what is left that you still want to know?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 10.5 is a verse from chapter 10 (Quiet). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "You are one, aware and pure. The world is inert and unreal. Not knowing is nothing either. So what is left that you still want to know?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: राज्यं सुताः कलत्राणि शरीराणि सुखानि च । संसक्तस्यापि नष्टानि तव जन्मनि जन्मनि ॥
verses.iast: rājyaṃ sutāḥ kalatrāṇi śarīrāṇi sukhāni ca | saṃsaktasyāpi naṣṭāni tava janmani janmani ||
verses.en: Kingdoms, sons, wives, bodies and pleasures: you were attached to them, and still you lost them, birth after birth.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 10.6 is a verse from chapter 10 (Quiet). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Kingdoms, sons, wives, bodies and pleasures: you were attached to them, and still you lost them, birth after birth."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: अलमर्थेन कामेन सुकृतेनापि कर्मणा । एभ्यः संसारकान्तारे न विश्रान्तमभून् मनः ॥
verses.iast: alamarthena kāmena sukṛtenāpi karmaṇā | ebhyaḥ saṃsārakāntāre na viśrāntamabhūn manaḥ ||
verses.en: Enough of wealth, desire and even good deeds. In the thick forest of the world, the mind found no rest in them.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 10.7 is a verse from chapter 10 (Quiet). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Enough of wealth, desire and even good deeds. In the thick forest of the world, the mind found no rest in them."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: कृतं न कति जन्मानि कायेन मनसा गिरा । दुःखमायासदं कर्म तदद्याप्युपरम्यताम् ॥
verses.iast: kṛtaṃ na kati janmāni kāyena manasā girā | duḥkhamāyāsadaṃ karma tadadyāpyuparamyatām ||
verses.en: For how many births have you done hard and painful work with body, mind and speech? Stop now, at least today.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 10.8 is a verse from chapter 10 (Quiet). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "For how many births have you done hard and painful work with body, mind and speech? Stop now, at least today."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: भावाभावविकारश्च स्वभावादिति निश्चयी । निर्विकारो गतक्लेशः सुखेनैवोपशाम्यति ॥
verses.iast: bhāvābhāvavikāraśca svabhāvāditi niścayī | nirvikāro gatakleśaḥ sukhenaivopaśāmyati ||
verses.en: Becoming, ceasing and change come from the nature of things. One who is sure of this stays unchanged, free of distress, and comes to rest with ease.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 11.1 is a verse from chapter 11 (Eight certainties). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Becoming, ceasing and change come from the nature of things. One who is sure of this stays unchanged, free of distress, and comes to rest with ease."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: ईश्वरः सर्वनिर्माता नेहान्य इति निश्चयी । अन्तर्गलितसर्वाशः शान्तः क्वापि न सज्जते ॥
verses.iast: īśvaraḥ sarvanirmātā nehānya iti niścayī | antargalitasarvāśaḥ śāntaḥ kvāpi na sajjate ||
verses.en: 'God is the maker of all, and there is none besides him here': one who is sure of this, every wish melted inside, is at peace and clings to nothing.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 11.2 is a verse from chapter 11 (Eight certainties). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "'God is the maker of all, and there is none besides him here': one who is sure of this, every wish melted inside, is at peace and clings to nothing."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: आपदः सम्पदः काले दैवादेवेति निश्चयी । तृप्तः स्वस्थेन्द्रियो नित्यं न वान्छति न शोचति ॥
verses.iast: āpadaḥ sampadaḥ kāle daivādeveti niścayī | tṛptaḥ svasthendriyo nityaṃ na vānchati na śocati ||
verses.en: Hard times and good times come in their season, by destiny. One who is sure of this is content, his senses at rest. He does not long and does not grieve.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 11.3 is a verse from chapter 11 (Eight certainties). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Hard times and good times come in their season, by destiny. One who is sure of this is content, his senses at rest. He does not long and does not grieve."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: सुखदुःखे जन्ममृत्यू दैवादेवेति निश्चयी । साध्यादर्शी निरायासः कुर्वन्नपि न लिप्यते ॥
verses.iast: sukhaduḥkhe janmamṛtyū daivādeveti niścayī | sādhyādarśī nirāyāsaḥ kurvannapi na lipyate ||
verses.en: Pleasure and pain, birth and death come by destiny. One who is sure of this sees nothing he must achieve, makes no strain, and is not stained even while acting.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 11.4 is a verse from chapter 11 (Eight certainties). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Pleasure and pain, birth and death come by destiny. One who is sure of this sees nothing he must achieve, makes no strain, and is not stained even while acting."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: चिन्तया जायते दुःखं नान्यथेहेति निश्चयी । तया हीनः सुखी शान्तः सर्वत्र गलितस्पृहः ॥
verses.iast: cintayā jāyate duḥkhaṃ nānyatheheti niścayī | tayā hīnaḥ sukhī śāntaḥ sarvatra galitaspṛhaḥ ||
verses.en: Sorrow is born of worry and of nothing else here. One who is sure of this is free of worry, happy, at peace, his wanting melted everywhere.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 11.5 is a verse from chapter 11 (Eight certainties). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Sorrow is born of worry and of nothing else here. One who is sure of this is free of worry, happy, at peace, his wanting melted everywhere."
verses.notice: The verse names one source of sorrow, worry, and adds 'and nothing else here'.
verses.commentary: Chapter 11 has eight verses, each built around niścayī, one who is certain. This one names worry, cintā, as the source of sorrow, and says nānyatheha, not otherwise, here. The claim is strong. Events happen, losses happen, but the sorrow that lingers and spreads is made of thought turning over and over. Someone waiting for a medical result knows this: the hours of waiting often hurt more than the news. The Advaita commentators do not tell the reader to stop thinking by force, which rarely works. They point to certainty. One who is sure of this, who has seen it in his own experience, is freed of worry by that seeing. Then three results follow, as in many verses of this text: happy, peaceful, and with wanting melted, galita-spṛha. The image of melting is gentle. Desire is left to soften and run off once the heat of worry is gone. The verse is a good one to read slowly, more than once, on an anxious evening.

bridge.note: Krishna asks how there can be happiness for one who has no peace.

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: नाहं देहो न मे देहो बोधोऽहमिति निश्चयी । कैवल्यमिव सम्प्राप्तो न स्मरत्यकृतं कृतम् ॥
verses.iast: nāhaṃ deho na me deho bodho'hamiti niścayī | kaivalyamiva samprāpto na smaratyakṛtaṃ kṛtam ||
verses.en: 'I am not the body, the body is not mine, I am awareness': one who is sure of this has reached something like final freedom. He does not keep count of what he did and left undone.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 11.6 is a verse from chapter 11 (Eight certainties). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "'I am not the body, the body is not mine, I am awareness': one who is sure of this has reached something like final freedom. He does not keep count of what he did and left undone."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: आब्रह्मस्तम्बपर्यन्तमहमेवेति निश्चयी । निर्विकल्पः शुचिः शान्तः प्राप्ताप्राप्तविनिर्वृतः ॥
verses.iast: ābrahmastambaparyantamahameveti niścayī | nirvikalpaḥ śuciḥ śāntaḥ prāptāprāptavinirvṛtaḥ ||
verses.en: 'From Brahma down to a clump of grass, it is all I': one who is sure of this has no wavering thought, is pure and at peace, and no longer worries about what he has and lacks.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 11.7 is a verse from chapter 11 (Eight certainties). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "'From Brahma down to a clump of grass, it is all I': one who is sure of this has no wavering thought, is pure and at peace, and no longer worries about what he has and lacks."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: नानाश्चर्यमिदं विश्वं न किञ्चिदिति निश्चयी । निर्वासनः स्फूर्तिमात्रो न किञ्चिदिव शाम्यति ॥
verses.iast: nānāścaryamidaṃ viśvaṃ na kiñciditi niścayī | nirvāsanaḥ sphūrtimātro na kiñcidiva śāmyati ||
verses.en: This world of many wonders is nothing: one who is sure of this is free of tendencies, awareness alone, and comes to rest as if nothing were there.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 11.8 is a verse from chapter 11 (Eight certainties). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "This world of many wonders is nothing: one who is sure of this is free of tendencies, awareness alone, and comes to rest as if nothing were there."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: कायकृत्यासहः पूर्वं ततो वाग्विस्तरासहः । अथ चिन्तासहस्तस्माद् एवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥
verses.iast: kāyakṛtyāsahaḥ pūrvaṃ tato vāgvistarāsahaḥ | atha cintāsahastasmād evamevāhamāsthitaḥ ||
verses.en: First I lost patience with the body's work, then with long talk, then with thinking itself. So I rest as I am.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 12.1 is a verse from chapter 12 (How I came to rest). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "First I lost patience with the body's work, then with long talk, then with thinking itself. So I rest as I am."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: प्रीत्यभावेन शब्दादेरदृश्यत्वेन चात्मनः । विक्षेपैकाग्रहृदय एवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥
verses.iast: prītyabhāvena śabdāderadṛśyatvena cātmanaḥ | vikṣepaikāgrahṛdaya evamevāhamāsthitaḥ ||
verses.en: Sound and the other objects no longer pull at me, and the Self is no object to be seen. My heart is free of scatter and gathered. So I rest as I am.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 12.2 is a verse from chapter 12 (How I came to rest). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Sound and the other objects no longer pull at me, and the Self is no object to be seen. My heart is free of scatter and gathered. So I rest as I am."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: समाध्यासादिविक्षिप्तौ व्यवहारः समाधये । एवं विलोक्य नियममेवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥
verses.iast: samādhyāsādivikṣiptau vyavahāraḥ samādhaye | evaṃ vilokya niyamamevamevāhamāsthitaḥ ||
verses.en: Distraction comes from taking things as real, and effort is then made to reach samadhi. Seeing that this is how it goes, I rest as I am.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 12.3 is a verse from chapter 12 (How I came to rest). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Distraction comes from taking things as real, and effort is then made to reach samadhi. Seeing that this is how it goes, I rest as I am."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: हेयोपादेयविरहाद् एवं हर्षविषादयोः । अभावादद्य हे ब्रह्मन्एवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥
verses.iast: heyopādeyavirahād evaṃ harṣaviṣādayoḥ | abhāvādadya he brahmanevamevāhamāsthitaḥ ||
verses.en: There is nothing to reject and nothing to take, so there is no joy and no sorrow. O Brahman, so I rest as I am.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 12.4 is a verse from chapter 12 (How I came to rest). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "There is nothing to reject and nothing to take, so there is no joy and no sorrow. O Brahman, so I rest as I am."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: आश्रमानाश्रमं ध्यानं चित्तस्वीकृतवर्जनम् । विकल्पं मम वीक्ष्यैतैरेवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥
verses.iast: āśramānāśramaṃ dhyānaṃ cittasvīkṛtavarjanam | vikalpaṃ mama vīkṣyaitairevamevāhamāsthitaḥ ||
verses.en: A stage of life or none, meditation, the mind taking things up and dropping them: seeing these as my own imaginings, I rest as I am.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 12.5 is a verse from chapter 12 (How I came to rest). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "A stage of life or none, meditation, the mind taking things up and dropping them: seeing these as my own imaginings, I rest as I am."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: कर्मानुष्ठानमज्ञानाद् यथैवोपरमस्तथा । बुध्वा सम्यगिदं तत्त्वमेवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥
verses.iast: karmānuṣṭhānamajñānād yathaivoparamastathā | budhvā samyagidaṃ tattvamevamevāhamāsthitaḥ ||
verses.en: Doing rituals comes from not knowing, and so does stopping them. Knowing this truth fully, I rest as I am.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 12.6 is a verse from chapter 12 (How I came to rest). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Doing rituals comes from not knowing, and so does stopping them. Knowing this truth fully, I rest as I am."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: अचिन्त्यं चिन्त्यमानोऽपि चिन्तारूपं भजत्यसौ । त्यक्त्वा तद्भावनं तस्माद् एवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥
verses.iast: acintyaṃ cintyamāno'pi cintārūpaṃ bhajatyasau | tyaktvā tadbhāvanaṃ tasmād evamevāhamāsthitaḥ ||
verses.en: Thinking about the unthinkable is still a form of thought. So I have let that thinking go, and rest as I am.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 12.7 is a verse from chapter 12 (How I came to rest). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Thinking about the unthinkable is still a form of thought. So I have let that thinking go, and rest as I am."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: एवमेव कृतं येन स कृतार्थो भवेदसौ । एवमेव स्वभावो यः स कृतार्थो भवेदसौ ॥
verses.iast: evameva kṛtaṃ yena sa kṛtārtho bhavedasau | evameva svabhāvo yaḥ sa kṛtārtho bhavedasau ||
verses.en: Whoever has done this has done all there is to do. Whoever is like this by nature has done all there is to do.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 12.8 is a verse from chapter 12 (How I came to rest). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Whoever has done this has done all there is to do. Whoever is like this by nature has done all there is to do."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: अकिञ्चनभवं स्वास्थं कौपीनत्वेऽपि दुर्लभम् । त्यागादाने विहायास्मादहमासे यथासुखम् ॥
verses.iast: akiñcanabhavaṃ svāsthaṃ kaupīnatve'pi durlabham | tyāgādāne vihāyāsmādahamāse yathāsukham ||
verses.en: The ease of owning nothing is rare even for one who wears only a loincloth. So I have left both giving up and taking, and live as it pleases me.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 13.1 is a verse from chapter 13 (As it pleases me). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "The ease of owning nothing is rare even for one who wears only a loincloth. So I have left both giving up and taking, and live as it pleases me."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: कुत्रापि खेदः कायस्य जिह्वा कुत्रापि खेद्यते । मनः कुत्रापि तत्त्यक्त्वा पुरुषार्थे स्थितः सुखम् ॥
verses.iast: kutrāpi khedaḥ kāyasya jihvā kutrāpi khedyate | manaḥ kutrāpi tattyaktvā puruṣārthe sthitaḥ sukham ||
verses.en: Here the body is strained, there the tongue grows tired, and there the mind. So I have left them and live at ease in what life is for.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 13.2 is a verse from chapter 13 (As it pleases me). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Here the body is strained, there the tongue grows tired, and there the mind. So I have left them and live at ease in what life is for."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: कृतं किमपि नैव स्याद् इति सञ्चिन्त्य तत्त्वतः । यदा यत्कर्तुमायाति तत् कृत्वासे यथासुखम् ॥
verses.iast: kṛtaṃ kimapi naiva syād iti sañcintya tattvataḥ | yadā yatkartumāyāti tat kṛtvāse yathāsukham ||
verses.en: Knowing as it is that nothing is ever done by the Self, I do whatever comes to be done and live as it pleases me.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 13.3 is a verse from chapter 13 (As it pleases me). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Knowing as it is that nothing is ever done by the Self, I do whatever comes to be done and live as it pleases me."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: कर्मनैष्कर्म्यनिर्बन्धभावा देहस्थयोगिनः । संयोगायोगविरहादहमासे यथासुखम् ॥
verses.iast: karmanaiṣkarmyanirbandhabhāvā dehasthayoginaḥ | saṃyogāyogavirahādahamāse yathāsukham ||
verses.en: Yogis who take themselves to be the body insist on action or on doing nothing. I am free of joining and parting, and live as it pleases me.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 13.4 is a verse from chapter 13 (As it pleases me). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Yogis who take themselves to be the body insist on action or on doing nothing. I am free of joining and parting, and live as it pleases me."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: अर्थानर्थौ न मे स्थित्या गत्या न शयनेन वा । तिष्ठन् गच्छन् स्वपन् तस्मादहमासे यथासुखम् ॥
verses.iast: arthānarthau na me sthityā gatyā na śayanena vā | tiṣṭhan gacchan svapan tasmādahamāse yathāsukham ||
verses.en: I gain nothing and lose nothing by standing, walking or lying down. So whether I stand, walk or sleep, I live as it pleases me.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 13.5 is a verse from chapter 13 (As it pleases me). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "I gain nothing and lose nothing by standing, walking or lying down. So whether I stand, walk or sleep, I live as it pleases me."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: स्वपतो नास्ति मे हानिः सिद्धिर्यत्नवतो न वा । नाशोल्लासौ विहायास्मादहमासे यथासुखम् ॥
verses.iast: svapato nāsti me hāniḥ siddhiryatnavato na vā | nāśollāsau vihāyāsmādahamāse yathāsukham ||
verses.en: Sleeping, I lose nothing. Striving, I win nothing. So I have dropped both loss and delight, and live as it pleases me.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 13.6 is a verse from chapter 13 (As it pleases me). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Sleeping, I lose nothing. Striving, I win nothing. So I have dropped both loss and delight, and live as it pleases me."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: सुखादिरूपा नियमं भावेष्वालोक्य भूरिशः । शुभाशुभे विहायास्मादहमासे यथासुखम् ॥
verses.iast: sukhādirūpā niyamaṃ bhāveṣvālokya bhūriśaḥ | śubhāśubhe vihāyāsmādahamāse yathāsukham ||
verses.en: Having seen many times how pleasure and the rest come and go in things, I have left good and bad behind, and live as it pleases me.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 13.7 is a verse from chapter 13 (As it pleases me). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Having seen many times how pleasure and the rest come and go in things, I have left good and bad behind, and live as it pleases me."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: प्रकृत्या शून्यचित्तो यः प्रमादाद् भावभावनः । निद्रितो बोधित इव क्षीणसंस्मरणो हि सः ॥
verses.iast: prakṛtyā śūnyacitto yaḥ pramādād bhāvabhāvanaḥ | nidrito bodhita iva kṣīṇasaṃsmaraṇo hi saḥ ||
verses.en: One whose mind is empty by nature, who thinks of things only by oversight, is like someone who has woken from sleep: his memories of the world have grown faint.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 14.1 is a verse from chapter 14 (Peace). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "One whose mind is empty by nature, who thinks of things only by oversight, is like someone who has woken from sleep: his memories of the world have grown faint."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: क्व धनानि क्व मित्राणि क्व मे विषयदस्यवः । क्व शास्त्रं क्व च विज्ञानं यदा मे गलिता स्पृहा ॥
verses.iast: kva dhanāni kva mitrāṇi kva me viṣayadasyavaḥ | kva śāstraṃ kva ca vijñānaṃ yadā me galitā spṛhā ||
verses.en: Where is wealth, where are friends, where are the thieves called sense objects, where is scripture, where is learning, now that my craving has melted away?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 14.2 is a verse from chapter 14 (Peace). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Where is wealth, where are friends, where are the thieves called sense objects, where is scripture, where is learning, now that my craving has melted away?"

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: विज्ञाते साक्षिपुरुषे परमात्मनि चेश्वरे । नैराश्ये बन्धमोक्षे च न चिन्ता मुक्तये मम ॥
verses.iast: vijñāte sākṣipuruṣe paramātmani ceśvare | nairāśye bandhamokṣe ca na cintā muktaye mama ||
verses.en: Now that I have known the witness, the supreme Self, the Lord, and hope for neither bondage nor freedom, I have no worry about being freed.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 14.3 is a verse from chapter 14 (Peace). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Now that I have known the witness, the supreme Self, the Lord, and hope for neither bondage nor freedom, I have no worry about being freed."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: अन्तर्विकल्पशून्यस्य बहिः स्वच्छन्दचारिणः । भ्रान्तस्येव दशास्तास्तास्तादृशा एव जानते ॥
verses.iast: antarvikalpaśūnyasya bahiḥ svacchandacāriṇaḥ | bhrāntasyeva daśāstāstāstādṛśā eva jānate ||
verses.en: Empty of wavering thoughts within, moving freely outside like someone confused: such states are known only by those who share them.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 14.4 is a verse from chapter 14 (Peace). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Empty of wavering thoughts within, moving freely outside like someone confused: such states are known only by those who share them."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: यथातथोपदेशेन कृतार्थः सत्त्वबुद्धिमान् । आजीवमपि जिज्ञासुः परस्तत्र विमुह्यति ॥
verses.iast: yathātathopadeśena kṛtārthaḥ sattvabuddhimān | ājīvamapi jijñāsuḥ parastatra vimuhyati ||
verses.en: A person of clear understanding is fulfilled by a teaching given in any way at all. Another may inquire his whole life and still stay confused.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 15.1 is a verse from chapter 15 (What you are). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "A person of clear understanding is fulfilled by a teaching given in any way at all. Another may inquire his whole life and still stay confused."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: मोक्षो विषयवैरस्यं बन्धो वैषयिको रसः । एतावदेव विज्ञानं यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
verses.iast: mokṣo viṣayavairasyaṃ bandho vaiṣayiko rasaḥ | etāvadeva vijñānaṃ yathecchasi tathā kuru ||
verses.en: Freedom is losing the taste for objects. Bondage is the taste for them. That is all there is to know. Now do as you wish.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 15.2 is a verse from chapter 15 (What you are). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Freedom is losing the taste for objects. Bondage is the taste for them. That is all there is to know. Now do as you wish."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: वाग्मिप्राज्ञामहोद्योगं जनं मूकजडालसम् । करोति तत्त्वबोधोऽयमतस्त्यक्तो बुभुक्षभिः ॥
verses.iast: vāgmiprājñāmahodyogaṃ janaṃ mūkajaḍālasam | karoti tattvabodho'yamatastyakto bubhukṣabhiḥ ||
verses.en: This knowing of the truth turns the talker, the clever and the busy into someone silent, still and idle. So those who want enjoyment avoid it.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 15.3 is a verse from chapter 15 (What you are). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "This knowing of the truth turns the talker, the clever and the busy into someone silent, still and idle. So those who want enjoyment avoid it."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: न त्वं देहो न ते देहो भोक्ता कर्ता न वा भवान् । चिद्रूपोऽसि सदा साक्षी निरपेक्षः सुखं चर ॥
verses.iast: na tvaṃ deho na te deho bhoktā kartā na vā bhavān | cidrūpo'si sadā sākṣī nirapekṣaḥ sukhaṃ cara ||
verses.en: You are not the body, and the body is not yours. You are not the doer or the enjoyer. You are awareness itself, always the witness, needing nothing. Move about at ease.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 15.4 is a verse from chapter 15 (What you are). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "You are not the body, and the body is not yours. You are not the doer or the enjoyer. You are awareness itself, always the witness, needing nothing. Move about at ease."
verses.notice: The verse begins with denials and ends with a walk: move about at ease.
verses.commentary: Chapter 15 returns to the themes of chapter 1, and this verse gathers the main points of chapter 1 into one line. You are not the body, and the body is not yours. You are neither doer nor enjoyer. You are awareness, always the witness, needing nothing. Then the instruction: sukhaṃ cara, move about at ease. Cara is a verb of walking, wandering, living one's life. It is a fitting end. The teaching sends Janaka back into his day with a lighter step, with no demand that he sit still forever. The phrase na te deha, the body is not yours, goes a step beyond na tvaṃ deha, you are not the body. Even ownership is denied. The Advaita reading is that the body belongs to nature and is used by awareness, the way a road is used by a traveller. The traveller does not own it and is not harmed when it ends. Readers who want one verse to memorise from the Ashtavakra Gita often choose this one.

bridge.note: Krishna says the Self is never born and never dies, and is not slain when the body is slain.

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: रागद्वेषौ मनोधर्मौ न मनस्ते कदाचन । निर्विकल्पोऽसि बोधात्मा निर्विकारः सुखं चर ॥
verses.iast: rāgadveṣau manodharmau na manaste kadācana | nirvikalpo'si bodhātmā nirvikāraḥ sukhaṃ cara ||
verses.en: Liking and disliking belong to the mind, and the mind was never yours. You are free of wavering, awareness itself, unchanging. Move about at ease.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 15.5 is a verse from chapter 15 (What you are). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Liking and disliking belong to the mind, and the mind was never yours. You are free of wavering, awareness itself, unchanging. Move about at ease."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि । विज्ञाय निरहङ्कारो निर्ममस्त्वं सुखी भव ॥
verses.iast: sarvabhūteṣu cātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani | vijñāya nirahaṅkāro nirmamastvaṃ sukhī bhava ||
verses.en: Know the Self in every being and every being in the Self. Free of 'I' and free of 'mine', be happy.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 15.6 is a verse from chapter 15 (What you are). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Know the Self in every being and every being in the Self. Free of 'I' and free of 'mine', be happy."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: विश्वं स्फुरति यत्रेदं तरङ्गा इव सागरे । तत्त्वमेव न सन्देहश्चिन्मूर्ते विज्वरो भव ॥
verses.iast: viśvaṃ sphurati yatredaṃ taraṅgā iva sāgare | tattvameva na sandehaścinmūrte vijvaro bhava ||
verses.en: That in which this world shimmers like waves on the sea: you are that, without doubt. You who are awareness, let the fever go.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 15.7 is a verse from chapter 15 (What you are). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "That in which this world shimmers like waves on the sea: you are that, without doubt. You who are awareness, let the fever go."
verses.notice: The line about waves on the sea, first used in 3.3 as a question, returns here as a plain statement.
verses.commentary: In chapter 3 Ashtavakra used the first half of this verse to scold Janaka: you know you are that in which the world rises like waves, so why do you run about like a pauper? Here, in chapter 15, the same half-line comes back without the scolding. That in which the world shimmers like waves on the sea: you are that, without doubt. Sphurati is a lovely verb. It means to flash, to quiver into view, the way light catches on moving water. The world is pictured as that kind of flicker on the surface of awareness. Then Ashtavakra calls Janaka cinmūrti, form of awareness, and tells him to be vijvara, free of fever. Jvara is the ordinary word for fever, and it is used for the restless heat of craving and worry. The Advaita reading treats the verse as close to the great Upanishadic sayings, such as tat tvam asi, you are that. It is spoken with confidence. Na sandehaḥ, there is no doubt.

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: श्रद्धस्व तात श्रद्धस्व नात्र मोऽहं कुरुष्व भोः । ज्ञानस्वरूपो भगवानात्मा त्वं प्रकृतेः परः ॥
verses.iast: śraddhasva tāta śraddhasva nātra mo'haṃ kuruṣva bhoḥ | jñānasvarūpo bhagavānātmā tvaṃ prakṛteḥ paraḥ ||
verses.en: Trust, my child, trust. Do not be confused about this. You are the Self, made of knowledge, the Lord, beyond nature.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 15.8 is a verse from chapter 15 (What you are). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Trust, my child, trust. Do not be confused about this. You are the Self, made of knowledge, the Lord, beyond nature."
verses.notice: Ashtavakra repeats one word, śraddhasva, trust, as a father would.
verses.commentary: This verse has a tenderness rare in the text. Ashtavakra says śraddhasva twice, trust, trust, and calls Janaka tāta, child, and bhoḥ, an affectionate address. Śraddhā in the Vedanta tradition is not blind belief. The Vivekachudamani, traditionally attributed to Shankara, defines it as holding the words of the teacher and the scripture to be true, a working confidence that lets you test what you hear. Without it nothing can be learned, since you will not stay with a teaching long enough to see whether it is true. The content of what is to be trusted is large. You are the Self, whose nature is knowledge, the Lord, beyond nature. Bhagavān is a word usually reserved for God. Ashtavakra uses it for Janaka's own Self without hesitation. The Advaita teachers say this is where knowledge and devotion meet: the Lord you worship and the Self you are turn out to be one. The verse asks the reader for something modest, which is to stop arguing with the teaching long enough to look.

bridge.note: Krishna says the one with trust, devoted and self-controlled, gains knowledge and soon reaches peace.

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: गुणैः संवेष्टितो देहस्तिष्ठत्यायाति याति च । आत्मा न गन्ता नागन्ता किमेनमनुशोचसि ॥
verses.iast: guṇaiḥ saṃveṣṭito dehastiṣṭhatyāyāti yāti ca | ātmā na gantā nāgantā kimenamanuśocasi ||
verses.en: The body, wrapped in the qualities of nature, comes, stays and goes. The Self neither goes nor comes. Why grieve over it?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 15.9 is a verse from chapter 15 (What you are). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The body, wrapped in the qualities of nature, comes, stays and goes. The Self neither goes nor comes. Why grieve over it?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: देहस्तिष्ठतु कल्पान्तं गच्छत्वद्यैव वा पुनः । क्व वृद्धिः क्व च वा हानिस्तव चिन्मात्ररूपिणः ॥
verses.iast: dehastiṣṭhatu kalpāntaṃ gacchatvadyaiva vā punaḥ | kva vṛddhiḥ kva ca vā hānistava cinmātrarūpiṇaḥ ||
verses.en: Let the body last to the end of the age or go today. What is gained or lost for you, who are awareness alone?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 15.10 is a verse from chapter 15 (What you are). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Let the body last to the end of the age or go today. What is gained or lost for you, who are awareness alone?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: त्वय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ विश्ववीचिः स्वभावतः । उदेतु वास्तमायातु न ते वृद्धिर्न वा क्षतिः ॥
verses.iast: tvayyanantamahāmbhodhau viśvavīciḥ svabhāvataḥ | udetu vāstamāyātu na te vṛddhirna vā kṣatiḥ ||
verses.en: In you, the endless ocean, the wave of the world rises or sinks by its own nature. You neither grow nor shrink.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 15.11 is a verse from chapter 15 (What you are). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "In you, the endless ocean, the wave of the world rises or sinks by its own nature. You neither grow nor shrink."
verses.notice: This is Janaka's own line from 7.2, given back to him by his teacher with 'I' changed to 'you'.
verses.commentary: In chapter 7 Janaka said: in me, the endless ocean, the wave of the world rises or sinks by its own nature, and I neither grow nor shrink. Here Ashtavakra says the same line with one change. In you. The teacher hands the student's insight back to him, confirmed. The verb forms matter. Udetu and astam āyātu are imperatives of permission: let it rise, let it set. There is no command to stop the wave or to ride it, only permission for it to do what it does. Then: na te vṛddhir na vā kṣatiḥ, there is no growth and no loss for you. Advaita teachers use this verse to describe a calm that does not depend on outcomes. A good year and a bad year are both waves. The ocean is not richer after a high tide. Someone who has watched savings go up and down, or a career rise and stall, can test the verse against that experience and see whether the one watching ever changed.

bridge.note: Krishna describes the ocean that stays unmoved while rivers pour into it, and the person at peace like it.

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: तात चिन्मात्ररूपोऽसि न ते भिन्नमिदं जगत् । अतः कस्य कथं कुत्र हेयोपादेयकल्पना ॥
verses.iast: tāta cinmātrarūpo'si na te bhinnamidaṃ jagat | ataḥ kasya kathaṃ kutra heyopādeyakalpanā ||
verses.en: My child, you are awareness alone. This world is not separate from you. So who could imagine anything to reject or take, and how, and where?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 15.12 is a verse from chapter 15 (What you are). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "My child, you are awareness alone. This world is not separate from you. So who could imagine anything to reject or take, and how, and where?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: एकस्मिन्नव्यये शान्ते चिदाकाशेऽमले त्वयि । कुतो जन्म कुतो कर्म कुतोऽहङ्कार एव च ॥
verses.iast: ekasminnavyaye śānte cidākāśe'male tvayi | kuto janma kuto karma kuto'haṅkāra eva ca ||
verses.en: In you, who are one, unchanging, at peace, a spotless sky of awareness, where is birth, where is action, where is the sense of 'I'?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 15.13 is a verse from chapter 15 (What you are). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "In you, who are one, unchanging, at peace, a spotless sky of awareness, where is birth, where is action, where is the sense of 'I'?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: यत्त्वं पश्यसि तत्रैकस्त्वमेव प्रतिभाससे । किं पृथक् भासते स्वर्णात् कटकाङ्गदनूपुरम् ॥
verses.iast: yattvaṃ paśyasi tatraikastvameva pratibhāsase | kiṃ pṛthak bhāsate svarṇāt kaṭakāṅgadanūpuram ||
verses.en: Whatever you see, you alone appear in it. Do bracelets, armlets and anklets appear as anything apart from the gold?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 15.14 is a verse from chapter 15 (What you are). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Whatever you see, you alone appear in it. Do bracelets, armlets and anklets appear as anything apart from the gold?"
verses.notice: Bracelets, armlets and anklets are three shapes, and there is only one gold.
verses.commentary: Indian households have long kept wealth as jewellery, and every family knows that a bracelet can be melted into an anklet without losing a gram of gold. Ashtavakra uses this everyday knowledge. Whatever you see, you alone appear there. Do the bracelet, the armlet and the anklet appear as something apart from the gold? Of course not. You may admire the shape, wear it on a different part of the body, call it by a different name, and the jeweller still weighs it as gold. The Advaita reading applies this to all experience. Trees, cities and people are different shapes, and what appears as all of them is awareness. The world keeps its variety, and a good jeweller cares a great deal about the shape. Beneath every difference there is a unity that is never lost. The example appeared in 2.10 with a single bracelet. Here three ornaments make the point that variety itself is no obstacle to oneness.

bridge.note: Krishna says the rare great soul is the one who sees that Vasudeva is all.

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: अयं सोऽहमयं नाहं विभागमिति सन्त्यज । सर्वमात्मेति निश्चित्य निःसङ्कल्पः सुखी भव ॥
verses.iast: ayaṃ so'hamayaṃ nāhaṃ vibhāgamiti santyaja | sarvamātmeti niścitya niḥsaṅkalpaḥ sukhī bhava ||
verses.en: Drop the division 'I am this, I am not that'. Be certain that all is the Self, make no more plans of the mind, and be happy.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 15.15 is a verse from chapter 15 (What you are). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Drop the division 'I am this, I am not that'. Be certain that all is the Self, make no more plans of the mind, and be happy."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: तवैवाज्ञानतो विश्वं त्वमेकः परमार्थतः । त्वत्तोऽन्यो नास्ति संसारी नासंसारी च कश्चन ॥
verses.iast: tavaivājñānato viśvaṃ tvamekaḥ paramārthataḥ | tvatto'nyo nāsti saṃsārī nāsaṃsārī ca kaścana ||
verses.en: Through your own not knowing, the world exists. In truth you alone are. There is no one apart from you, bound to the world or free of it.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 15.16 is a verse from chapter 15 (What you are). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Through your own not knowing, the world exists. In truth you alone are. There is no one apart from you, bound to the world or free of it."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: भ्रान्तिमात्रमिदं विश्वं न किञ्चिदिति निश्चयी । निर्वासनः स्फूर्तिमात्रो न किञ्चिदिव शाम्यति ॥
verses.iast: bhrāntimātramidaṃ viśvaṃ na kiñciditi niścayī | nirvāsanaḥ sphūrtimātro na kiñcidiva śāmyati ||
verses.en: 'This world is only an error, it is nothing': one who is sure of this is free of tendencies, awareness alone, and comes to rest as if nothing were there.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 15.17 is a verse from chapter 15 (What you are). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "'This world is only an error, it is nothing': one who is sure of this is free of tendencies, awareness alone, and comes to rest as if nothing were there."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: एक एव भवाम्भोधावासीदस्ति भविष्यति । न ते बन्धोऽस्ति मोक्षो वा कृत्यकृत्यः सुखं चर ॥
verses.iast: eka eva bhavāmbhodhāvāsīdasti bhaviṣyati | na te bandho'sti mokṣo vā kṛtyakṛtyaḥ sukhaṃ cara ||
verses.en: In the ocean of the world there was one, there is one, there will be one: you. You have no bondage and no freedom. Your work is done. Move about at ease.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 15.18 is a verse from chapter 15 (What you are). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "In the ocean of the world there was one, there is one, there will be one: you. You have no bondage and no freedom. Your work is done. Move about at ease."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: मा सङ्कल्पविकल्पाभ्यां चित्तं क्षोभय चिन्मय । उपशाम्य सुखं तिष्ठ स्वात्मन्यानन्दविग्रहे ॥
verses.iast: mā saṅkalpavikalpābhyāṃ cittaṃ kṣobhaya cinmaya | upaśāmya sukhaṃ tiṣṭha svātmanyānandavigrahe ||
verses.en: You who are awareness, do not stir the mind with 'yes' and 'no'. Be still, and rest at ease in your own Self, which is joy itself.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 15.19 is a verse from chapter 15 (What you are). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "You who are awareness, do not stir the mind with 'yes' and 'no'. Be still, and rest at ease in your own Self, which is joy itself."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: त्यजैव ध्यानं सर्वत्र मा किञ्चिद् हृदि धारय । आत्मा त्वं मुक्त एवासि किं विमृश्य करिष्यसि ॥
verses.iast: tyajaiva dhyānaṃ sarvatra mā kiñcid hṛdi dhāraya | ātmā tvaṃ mukta evāsi kiṃ vimṛśya kariṣyasi ||
verses.en: Give up meditation altogether. Hold nothing in the heart. You are the Self, free already. What will you gain by thinking it over?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 15.20 is a verse from chapter 15 (What you are). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Give up meditation altogether. Hold nothing in the heart. You are the Self, free already. What will you gain by thinking it over?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: आचक्ष्व शृणु वा तात नानाशास्त्राण्यनेकशः । तथापि न तव स्वास्थ्यं सर्वविस्मरणाद् ऋते ॥
verses.iast: ācakṣva śṛṇu vā tāta nānāśāstrāṇyanekaśaḥ | tathāpi na tava svāsthyaṃ sarvavismaraṇād ṛte ||
verses.en: My child, you may recite many scriptures or hear them many times. Still you will not be at ease until you forget it all.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 16.1 is a verse from chapter 16 (Forget it all). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "My child, you may recite many scriptures or hear them many times. Still you will not be at ease until you forget it all."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: भोगं कर्म समाधिं वा कुरु विज्ञ तथापि ते । चित्तं निरस्तसर्वाशमत्यर्थं रोचयिष्यति ॥
verses.iast: bhogaṃ karma samādhiṃ vā kuru vijña tathāpi te | cittaṃ nirastasarvāśamatyarthaṃ rocayiṣyati ||
verses.en: Wise one, you may enjoy, work or sit in samadhi. Even so, your mind will long most of all for the place where every wish has ended.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 16.2 is a verse from chapter 16 (Forget it all). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Wise one, you may enjoy, work or sit in samadhi. Even so, your mind will long most of all for the place where every wish has ended."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: आयासात्सकलो दुःखी नैनं जानाति कश्चन । अनेनैवोपदेशेन धन्यः प्राप्नोति निर्वृतिम् ॥
verses.iast: āyāsātsakalo duḥkhī nainaṃ jānāti kaścana | anenaivopadeśena dhanyaḥ prāpnoti nirvṛtim ||
verses.en: Everyone suffers from effort, and nobody sees it. By this teaching alone, the fortunate one finds rest.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 16.3 is a verse from chapter 16 (Forget it all). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Everyone suffers from effort, and nobody sees it. By this teaching alone, the fortunate one finds rest."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: व्यापारे खिद्यते यस्तु निमेषोन्मेषयोरपि । तस्यालस्य धुरीणस्य सुखं नन्यस्य कस्यचित् ॥
verses.iast: vyāpāre khidyate yastu nimeṣonmeṣayorapi | tasyālasya dhurīṇasya sukhaṃ nanyasya kasyacit ||
verses.en: The master idler, who finds even opening and closing his eyes a strain, has happiness. Nobody else has it.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 16.4 is a verse from chapter 16 (Forget it all). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The master idler, who finds even opening and closing his eyes a strain, has happiness. Nobody else has it."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: इदं कृतमिदं नेति द्वन्द्वैर्मुक्तं यदा मनः । धर्मार्थकाममोक्षेषु निरपेक्षं तदा भवेत् ॥
verses.iast: idaṃ kṛtamidaṃ neti dvandvairmuktaṃ yadā manaḥ | dharmārthakāmamokṣeṣu nirapekṣaṃ tadā bhavet ||
verses.en: When the mind is free of opposites like 'this is done, this is not done', it stops caring about dharma, wealth, pleasure and even freedom.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 16.5 is a verse from chapter 16 (Forget it all). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "When the mind is free of opposites like 'this is done, this is not done', it stops caring about dharma, wealth, pleasure and even freedom."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: विरक्तो विषयद्वेष्टा रागी विषयलोलुपः । ग्रहमोक्षविहीनस्तु न विरक्तो न रागवान् ॥
verses.iast: virakto viṣayadveṣṭā rāgī viṣayalolupaḥ | grahamokṣavihīnastu na virakto na rāgavān ||
verses.en: One who hates objects is dispassionate. One who craves them is attached. One who neither takes nor drops is neither dispassionate nor attached.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 16.6 is a verse from chapter 16 (Forget it all). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "One who hates objects is dispassionate. One who craves them is attached. One who neither takes nor drops is neither dispassionate nor attached."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: हेयोपादेयता तावत्संसारविटपाङ्कुरः । स्पृहा जीवति यावद् वै निर्विचारदशास्पदम् ॥
verses.iast: heyopādeyatā tāvatsaṃsāraviṭapāṅkuraḥ | spṛhā jīvati yāvad vai nirvicāradaśāspadam ||
verses.en: As long as wanting lives, which is a state without discernment, the sense of things to take and things to drop stays alive: the sprout of the tree of the world.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 16.7 is a verse from chapter 16 (Forget it all). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "As long as wanting lives, which is a state without discernment, the sense of things to take and things to drop stays alive: the sprout of the tree of the world."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: प्रवृत्तौ जायते रागो निर्वृत्तौ द्वेष एव हि । निर्द्वन्द्वो बालवद् धीमान् एवमेव व्यवस्थितः ॥
verses.iast: pravṛttau jāyate rāgo nirvṛttau dveṣa eva hi | nirdvandvo bālavad dhīmān evameva vyavasthitaḥ ||
verses.en: Activity breeds attachment, and holding back breeds aversion. So the wise one, free of opposites like a child, stays just as he is.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 16.8 is a verse from chapter 16 (Forget it all). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Activity breeds attachment, and holding back breeds aversion. So the wise one, free of opposites like a child, stays just as he is."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: हातुमिच्छति संसारं रागी दुःखजिहासया । वीतरागो हि निर्दुःखस्तस्मिन्नपि न खिद्यति ॥
verses.iast: hātumicchati saṃsāraṃ rāgī duḥkhajihāsayā | vītarāgo hi nirduḥkhastasminnapi na khidyati ||
verses.en: The attached person wants to leave the world to escape sorrow. One without attachment is free of sorrow and is not troubled even while living in it.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 16.9 is a verse from chapter 16 (Forget it all). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The attached person wants to leave the world to escape sorrow. One without attachment is free of sorrow and is not troubled even while living in it."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: यस्याभिमानो मोक्षेऽपि देहेऽपि ममता तथा । न च ज्ञानी न वा योगी केवलं दुःखभागसौ ॥
verses.iast: yasyābhimāno mokṣe'pi dehe'pi mamatā tathā | na ca jñānī na vā yogī kevalaṃ duḥkhabhāgasau ||
verses.en: One who takes pride even in freedom and still calls the body his own is neither a knower nor a yogi. He only shares in sorrow.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 16.10 is a verse from chapter 16 (Forget it all). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "One who takes pride even in freedom and still calls the body his own is neither a knower nor a yogi. He only shares in sorrow."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: हरो यद्युपदेष्टा ते हरिः कमलजोऽपि वा । तथापि न तव स्वाथ्यं सर्वविस्मरणादृते ॥
verses.iast: haro yadyupadeṣṭā te hariḥ kamalajo'pi vā | tathāpi na tava svāthyaṃ sarvavismaraṇādṛte ||
verses.en: Even if Shiva, Vishnu or lotus-born Brahma were your teacher, you would not be at ease until you forget it all.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 16.11 is a verse from chapter 16 (Forget it all). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Even if Shiva, Vishnu or lotus-born Brahma were your teacher, you would not be at ease until you forget it all."
verses.notice: Even the three highest gods as teachers would not be enough without forgetting.
verses.commentary: Chapter 16 opens and closes with the same refrain: you will not be at ease until you forget everything. In this last verse Ashtavakra raises the stakes. Even if Shiva, Vishnu or Brahma were your teacher, it would not be enough. The word for ease is svāsthya, literally standing in oneself, the same root as the modern Hindi word for health. What is to be forgotten is everything learned, believed and held as a position. The Advaita reading is careful here. Ashtavakra quotes scripture and relies on it, and he names the gods with respect. His point is that knowledge held as information keeps you outside of what it describes. A person who has memorised every map of a city still has to put the maps away to walk its streets. The verse is useful for anyone who reads a great deal about spiritual matters, this page included. At some point the reading has to stop and the resting has to begin.

bridge.note: Krishna says that when your understanding crosses the thicket of confusion, you will grow indifferent to all you have heard and will hear.

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: तेन ज्ञानफलं प्राप्तं योगाभ्यासफलं तथा । तृप्तः स्वच्छेन्द्रियो नित्यमेकाकी रमते तु यः ॥
verses.iast: tena jñānaphalaṃ prāptaṃ yogābhyāsaphalaṃ tathā | tṛptaḥ svacchendriyo nityamekākī ramate tu yaḥ ||
verses.en: He has the fruit of knowledge and the fruit of yoga practice who is content, whose senses are clear, and who delights in being alone.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 17.1 is a verse from chapter 17 (The one who knows). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "He has the fruit of knowledge and the fruit of yoga practice who is content, whose senses are clear, and who delights in being alone."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: न कदाचिज्जगत्यस्मिन् तत्त्वज्ञो हन्त खिद्यति । यत एकेन तेनेदं पूर्णं ब्रह्माण्डमण्डलम् ॥
verses.iast: na kadācijjagatyasmin tattvajño hanta khidyati | yata ekena tenedaṃ pūrṇaṃ brahmāṇḍamaṇḍalam ||
verses.en: One who knows what is real is never troubled here, for this whole round of worlds is filled by him alone.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 17.2 is a verse from chapter 17 (The one who knows). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "One who knows what is real is never troubled here, for this whole round of worlds is filled by him alone."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: न जातु विषयाः केऽपि स्वारामं हर्षयन्त्यमी । सल्लकीपल्लवप्रीतमिवेभं निम्बपल्लवाः ॥
verses.iast: na jātu viṣayāḥ ke'pi svārāmaṃ harṣayantyamī | sallakīpallavaprītamivebhaṃ nimbapallavāḥ ||
verses.en: No objects ever please one who delights in the Self, as neem leaves do not please an elephant who loves sallaki leaves.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 17.3 is a verse from chapter 17 (The one who knows). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "No objects ever please one who delights in the Self, as neem leaves do not please an elephant who loves sallaki leaves."
verses.notice: An elephant that loves sallaki leaves will not touch bitter neem.

words.m: one who delights in the Self
sallaki leaves, a tree elephants love

verses.commentary: Sallaki is the Indian frankincense tree, Boswellia, whose leaves elephants love. Neem leaves are bitter. An elephant that has its fill of sallaki will not bother with neem. Ashtavakra says sense objects are like neem to one who delights in the Self, svārāma. They are simply not interesting. The image avoids two common mistakes. It does not say the knower fights his desires, and it does not say objects are evil. Neem is a useful tree. It just has nothing to offer an elephant that has better food. The Advaita teachers read this as the natural end of desire, which comes from tasting something more satisfying. The Bhagavad Gita says the same thing in its second chapter: objects fall away from one who fasts, but the taste for them remains until the highest is seen. People searching for 'Ashtavakra Gita 17.3' often land on Bhagavad Gita 17.3, which is about faith shaping a person. This is the verse they were looking for.

bridge.note: Krishna says even the taste for objects falls away once the highest has been seen.

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: यस्तु भोगेषु भुक्तेषु न भवत्यधिवासितः । अभुक्तेषु निराकाङ्क्षी तदृशो भवदुर्लभः ॥
verses.iast: yastu bhogeṣu bhukteṣu na bhavatyadhivāsitaḥ | abhukteṣu nirākāṅkṣī tadṛśo bhavadurlabhaḥ ||
verses.en: One who does not dwell on pleasures he has had and does not long for those he has not had: such a person is rare.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 17.4 is a verse from chapter 17 (The one who knows). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "One who does not dwell on pleasures he has had and does not long for those he has not had: such a person is rare."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: बुभुक्षुरिह संसारे मुमुक्षुरपि दृश्यते । भोगमोक्षनिराकाङ्क्षी विरलो हि महाशयः ॥
verses.iast: bubhukṣuriha saṃsāre mumukṣurapi dṛśyate | bhogamokṣanirākāṅkṣī viralo hi mahāśayaḥ ||
verses.en: Here we see people who want enjoyment and people who want freedom. Rare is the great soul who wants neither.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 17.5 is a verse from chapter 17 (The one who knows). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Here we see people who want enjoyment and people who want freedom. Rare is the great soul who wants neither."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: धर्मार्थकाममोक्षेषु जीविते मरणे तथा । कस्याप्युदारचित्तस्य हेयोपादेयता न हि ॥
verses.iast: dharmārthakāmamokṣeṣu jīvite maraṇe tathā | kasyāpyudāracittasya heyopādeyatā na hi ||
verses.en: Rare is the large-hearted person who has no sense of taking or rejecting dharma, wealth, pleasure, freedom, life or death.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 17.6 is a verse from chapter 17 (The one who knows). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Rare is the large-hearted person who has no sense of taking or rejecting dharma, wealth, pleasure, freedom, life or death."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: वाञ्छा न विश्वविलये न द्वेषस्तस्य च स्थितौ । यथा जीविकया तस्माद् धन्य आस्ते यथा सुखम् ॥
verses.iast: vāñchā na viśvavilaye na dveṣastasya ca sthitau | yathā jīvikayā tasmād dhanya āste yathā sukham ||
verses.en: He has no wish for the world to end and no dislike of its going on. So the fortunate one lives at ease on whatever livelihood comes.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 17.7 is a verse from chapter 17 (The one who knows). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "He has no wish for the world to end and no dislike of its going on. So the fortunate one lives at ease on whatever livelihood comes."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: कृतार्थोऽनेन ज्ञानेनेत्येवं गलितधीः कृती । पश्यन् शृण्वन् स्पृशन् जिघ्रन्अश्नन्नास्ते यथा सुखम् ॥
verses.iast: kṛtārtho'nena jñānenetyevaṃ galitadhīḥ kṛtī | paśyan śṛṇvan spṛśan jighranaśnannāste yathā sukham ||
verses.en: Fulfilled by this knowledge, his mind melted away, he lives at ease, seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 17.8 is a verse from chapter 17 (The one who knows). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Fulfilled by this knowledge, his mind melted away, he lives at ease, seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: शून्या दृष्टिर्वृथा चेष्टा विकलानीन्द्रियाणि च । न स्पृहा न विरक्तिर्वा क्षीणसंसारसागरे ॥
verses.iast: śūnyā dṛṣṭirvṛthā ceṣṭā vikalānīndriyāṇi ca | na spṛhā na viraktirvā kṣīṇasaṃsārasāgare ||
verses.en: For one whose ocean of the world has dried up, the gaze is empty, action has no aim, the senses are idle. There is no wanting and no turning away.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 17.9 is a verse from chapter 17 (The one who knows). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "For one whose ocean of the world has dried up, the gaze is empty, action has no aim, the senses are idle. There is no wanting and no turning away."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: न जागर्ति न निद्राति नोन्मीलति न मीलति । अहो परदशा क्वापि वर्तते मुक्तचेतसः ॥
verses.iast: na jāgarti na nidrāti nonmīlati na mīlati | aho paradaśā kvāpi vartate muktacetasaḥ ||
verses.en: He is not awake and not asleep, he neither opens nor closes his eyes. How wonderful: the free mind lives in the highest state wherever it is.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 17.10 is a verse from chapter 17 (The one who knows). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "He is not awake and not asleep, he neither opens nor closes his eyes. How wonderful: the free mind lives in the highest state wherever it is."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: सर्वत्र दृश्यते स्वस्थः सर्वत्र विमलाशयः । समस्तवासना मुक्तो मुक्तः सर्वत्र राजते ॥
verses.iast: sarvatra dṛśyate svasthaḥ sarvatra vimalāśayaḥ | samastavāsanā mukto muktaḥ sarvatra rājate ||
verses.en: The free one is seen at ease everywhere, clear-hearted everywhere. Free of all tendencies, he shines everywhere.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 17.11 is a verse from chapter 17 (The one who knows). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The free one is seen at ease everywhere, clear-hearted everywhere. Free of all tendencies, he shines everywhere."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: पश्यन् शृण्वन् स्पृशन् जिघ्रन्अश्नन् गृण्हन् वदन् व्रजन् । ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो मुक्त एव महाशयः ॥
verses.iast: paśyan śṛṇvan spṛśan jighranaśnan gṛṇhan vadan vrajan | īhitānīhitairmukto mukta eva mahāśayaḥ ||
verses.en: Seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, taking, speaking, walking, free of wanting and not wanting, the great soul is free.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 17.12 is a verse from chapter 17 (The one who knows). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, taking, speaking, walking, free of wanting and not wanting, the great soul is free."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: न निन्दति न च स्तौति न हृष्यति न कुप्यति । न ददाति न गृण्हाति मुक्तः सर्वत्र नीरसः ॥
verses.iast: na nindati na ca stauti na hṛṣyati na kupyati | na dadāti na gṛṇhāti muktaḥ sarvatra nīrasaḥ ||
verses.en: He does not blame and does not praise, is not elated and is not angry, does not give and does not take. The free one has no taste for anything.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 17.13 is a verse from chapter 17 (The one who knows). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "He does not blame and does not praise, is not elated and is not angry, does not give and does not take. The free one has no taste for anything."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: सानुरागां स्त्रियं दृष्ट्वा मृत्युं वा समुपस्थितम् । अविह्वलमनाः स्वस्थो मुक्त एव महाशयः ॥
verses.iast: sānurāgāṃ striyaṃ dṛṣṭvā mṛtyuṃ vā samupasthitam | avihvalamanāḥ svastho mukta eva mahāśayaḥ ||
verses.en: Whether he sees a woman full of desire or death standing near, the great soul stays unshaken and at ease. He is free.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 17.14 is a verse from chapter 17 (The one who knows). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Whether he sees a woman full of desire or death standing near, the great soul stays unshaken and at ease. He is free."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: सुखे दुःखे नरे नार्यां सम्पत्सु च विपत्सु च । विशेषो नैव धीरस्य सर्वत्र समदर्शिनः ॥
verses.iast: sukhe duḥkhe nare nāryāṃ sampatsu ca vipatsu ca | viśeṣo naiva dhīrasya sarvatra samadarśinaḥ ||
verses.en: In pleasure and pain, man and woman, good fortune and bad, the steady one, who sees the same everywhere, finds no difference.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 17.15 is a verse from chapter 17 (The one who knows). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "In pleasure and pain, man and woman, good fortune and bad, the steady one, who sees the same everywhere, finds no difference."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: न हिंसा नैव कारुण्यं नौद्धत्यं न च दीनता । नाश्चर्यं नैव च क्षोभः क्षीणसंसरणे नरे ॥
verses.iast: na hiṃsā naiva kāruṇyaṃ nauddhatyaṃ na ca dīnatā | nāścaryaṃ naiva ca kṣobhaḥ kṣīṇasaṃsaraṇe nare ||
verses.en: In one whose round of births is worn out there is no cruelty and no pity, no arrogance and no meekness, no wonder and no agitation.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 17.16 is a verse from chapter 17 (The one who knows). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "In one whose round of births is worn out there is no cruelty and no pity, no arrogance and no meekness, no wonder and no agitation."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: न मुक्तो विषयद्वेष्टा न वा विषयलोलुपः । असंसक्तमना नित्यं प्राप्ताप्राप्तमुपाश्नुते ॥
verses.iast: na mukto viṣayadveṣṭā na vā viṣayalolupaḥ | asaṃsaktamanā nityaṃ prāptāprāptamupāśnute ||
verses.en: The free one neither hates objects nor craves them. With a mind always unattached, he takes what comes and what does not.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 17.17 is a verse from chapter 17 (The one who knows). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The free one neither hates objects nor craves them. With a mind always unattached, he takes what comes and what does not."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: समाधानसमाधानहिताहितविकल्पनाः । शून्यचित्तो न जानाति कैवल्यमिव संस्थितः ॥
