verses.iast: samādhānasamādhānahitāhitavikalpanāḥ | śūnyacitto na jānāti kaivalyamiva saṃsthitaḥ ||
verses.en: Gathered or scattered, good or bad: one whose mind is empty does not know these choices. He stays as if in final freedom.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 17.18 is a verse from chapter 17 (The one who knows). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Gathered or scattered, good or bad: one whose mind is empty does not know these choices. He stays as if in final freedom."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: निर्ममो निरहङ्कारो न किञ्चिदिति निश्चितः । अन्तर्गलितसर्वाशः कुर्वन्नपि करोति न ॥
verses.iast: nirmamo nirahaṅkāro na kiñciditi niścitaḥ | antargalitasarvāśaḥ kurvannapi karoti na ||
verses.en: Without 'mine', without 'I', certain that nothing is, every wish melted within, he does not act even while acting.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 17.19 is a verse from chapter 17 (The one who knows). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Without 'mine', without 'I', certain that nothing is, every wish melted within, he does not act even while acting."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: मनःप्रकाशसंमोहस्वप्नजाड्यविवर्जितः । दशां कामपि सम्प्राप्तो भवेद् गलितमानसः ॥
verses.iast: manaḥprakāśasaṃmohasvapnajāḍyavivarjitaḥ | daśāṃ kāmapi samprāpto bhaved galitamānasaḥ ||
verses.en: Free of the play of mind, confusion, dream and dullness, one whose mind has melted reaches a state nobody can name.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 17.20 is a verse from chapter 17 (The one who knows). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Free of the play of mind, confusion, dream and dullness, one whose mind has melted reaches a state nobody can name."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: यस्य बोधोदये तावत्स्वप्नवद् भवति भ्रमः । तस्मै सुखैकरूपाय नमः शान्ताय तेजसे ॥
verses.iast: yasya bodhodaye tāvatsvapnavad bhavati bhramaḥ | tasmai sukhaikarūpāya namaḥ śāntāya tejase ||
verses.en: I bow to that peace, that light, whose nature is joy alone, at whose dawning the error of the world becomes like a dream.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.1 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "I bow to that peace, that light, whose nature is joy alone, at whose dawning the error of the world becomes like a dream."
verses.notice: The hundred-verse chapter opens with a bow, before any argument.
verses.commentary: Chapter 18 is a hundred verses long, a third of the whole text, and it is often titled the chapter of peace. It opens with a salutation, namaḥ. What is saluted has no name: it is that light, tejas, that peace, śānta, whose one form is joy, at whose dawning the error of the world becomes like a dream. Dreams are the tradition's favourite evidence. While dreaming, the dream world is fully real, with its fears and pleasures. On waking, nothing of it needs to be destroyed. It simply stops being taken as real. The verse says the same happens to the world when awareness dawns. The Advaita commentators note that the bow is directed at what Ashtavakra has been teaching all along, the Self, so the teacher bows to the student's own nature before speaking. A reader can use the verse the same way, as a short act of respect at the start of a day, directed at the awareness that is about to see it.

bridge.note: Krishna says what is night for all beings is where the self-controlled one is awake.

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: अर्जयित्वाखिलान् अर्थान् भोगानाप्नोति पुष्कलान् । न हि सर्वपरित्यागमन्तरेण सुखी भवेत् ॥
verses.iast: arjayitvākhilān arthān bhogānāpnoti puṣkalān | na hi sarvaparityāgamantareṇa sukhī bhavet ||
verses.en: One may gain every kind of wealth and enjoy pleasures in plenty, yet nobody is happy without letting go of everything.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.2 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "One may gain every kind of wealth and enjoy pleasures in plenty, yet nobody is happy without letting go of everything."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: कर्तव्यदुःखमार्तण्डज्वालादग्धान्तरात्मनः । कुतः प्रशमपीयूषधारासारमृते सुखम् ॥
verses.iast: kartavyaduḥkhamārtaṇḍajvālādagdhāntarātmanaḥ | kutaḥ praśamapīyūṣadhārāsāramṛte sukham ||
verses.en: One whose inner self is scorched by the sun of duty and its pain: how can he be happy without the steady rain of the nectar of calm?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.3 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "One whose inner self is scorched by the sun of duty and its pain: how can he be happy without the steady rain of the nectar of calm?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: भवोऽयं भावनामात्रो न किञ्चित् परमर्थतः । नास्त्यभावः स्वभावानां भावाभावविभाविनाम् ॥
verses.iast: bhavo'yaṃ bhāvanāmātro na kiñcit paramarthataḥ | nāstyabhāvaḥ svabhāvānāṃ bhāvābhāvavibhāvinām ||
verses.en: This world is only a thought. In the highest truth it is nothing. That which is real by nature, and which lights up both being and not-being, never stops being.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.4 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "This world is only a thought. In the highest truth it is nothing. That which is real by nature, and which lights up both being and not-being, never stops being."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: न दूरं न च सङ्कोचाल्लब्धमेवात्मनः पदम् । निर्विकल्पं निरायासं निर्विकारं निरञ्जनम् ॥
verses.iast: na dūraṃ na ca saṅkocāllabdhamevātmanaḥ padam | nirvikalpaṃ nirāyāsaṃ nirvikāraṃ nirañjanam ||
verses.en: The place of the Self is near, and narrowing down does not gain it, for it is already yours: without thought, without effort, without change, without stain.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.5 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The place of the Self is near, and narrowing down does not gain it, for it is already yours: without thought, without effort, without change, without stain."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: व्यामोहमात्रविरतौ स्वरूपादानमात्रतः । वीतशोका विराजन्ते निरावरणदृष्टयः ॥
verses.iast: vyāmohamātraviratau svarūpādānamātrataḥ | vītaśokā virājante nirāvaraṇadṛṣṭayaḥ ||
verses.en: When confusion stops and one simply takes up one's own nature, people shine free of sorrow, their sight unveiled.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.6 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "When confusion stops and one simply takes up one's own nature, people shine free of sorrow, their sight unveiled."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: समस्तं कल्पनामात्रमात्मा मुक्तः सनातनः । इति विज्ञाय धीरो हि किमभ्यस्यति बालवत् ॥
verses.iast: samastaṃ kalpanāmātramātmā muktaḥ sanātanaḥ | iti vijñāya dhīro hi kimabhyasyati bālavat ||
verses.en: All this is only imagining. The Self is free and eternal. Knowing this, why would the steady one practise like a child?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.7 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "All this is only imagining. The Self is free and eternal. Knowing this, why would the steady one practise like a child?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: आत्मा ब्रह्मेति निश्चित्य भावाभावौ च कल्पितौ । निष्कामः किं विजानाति किं ब्रूते च करोति किम् ॥
verses.iast: ātmā brahmeti niścitya bhāvābhāvau ca kalpitau | niṣkāmaḥ kiṃ vijānāti kiṃ brūte ca karoti kim ||
verses.en: Certain that the Self is Brahman and that being and not-being are imagined, what does the one without desire need to know, say or do?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.8 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Certain that the Self is Brahman and that being and not-being are imagined, what does the one without desire need to know, say or do?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: अयं सोऽहमयं नाहमिति क्षीणा विकल्पना । सर्वमात्मेति निश्चित्य तूष्णीम्भूतस्य योगिनः ॥
verses.iast: ayaṃ so'hamayaṃ nāhamiti kṣīṇā vikalpanā | sarvamātmeti niścitya tūṣṇīmbhūtasya yoginaḥ ||
verses.en: 'I am this, I am not that': such thoughts fade for the yogi who is certain that all is the Self and has fallen silent.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.9 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "'I am this, I am not that': such thoughts fade for the yogi who is certain that all is the Self and has fallen silent."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: न विक्षेपो न चैकाग्र्यं नातिबोधो न मूढता । न सुखं न च वा दुःखमुपशान्तस्य योगिनः ॥
verses.iast: na vikṣepo na caikāgryaṃ nātibodho na mūḍhatā | na sukhaṃ na ca vā duḥkhamupaśāntasya yoginaḥ ||
verses.en: For the yogi at peace there is no distraction and no focus, no heightened knowing and no dullness, no pleasure and no pain.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.10 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "For the yogi at peace there is no distraction and no focus, no heightened knowing and no dullness, no pleasure and no pain."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: स्वाराज्ये भैक्षवृत्तौ च लाभालाभे जने वने । निर्विकल्पस्वभावस्य न विशेषोऽस्ति योगिनः ॥
verses.iast: svārājye bhaikṣavṛttau ca lābhālābhe jane vane | nirvikalpasvabhāvasya na viśeṣo'sti yoginaḥ ||
verses.en: Ruling a kingdom or living on alms, gain or loss, among people or in the forest: it makes no difference to the yogi whose nature is free of wavering thought.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.11 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Ruling a kingdom or living on alms, gain or loss, among people or in the forest: it makes no difference to the yogi whose nature is free of wavering thought."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: क्व धर्मः क्व च वा कामः क्व चार्थः क्व विवेकिता । इदं कृतमिदं नेति द्वन्द्वैर्मुक्तस्य योगिनः ॥
verses.iast: kva dharmaḥ kva ca vā kāmaḥ kva cārthaḥ kva vivekitā | idaṃ kṛtamidaṃ neti dvandvairmuktasya yoginaḥ ||
verses.en: Where is dharma, where is pleasure, where is wealth, where is discernment, for the yogi free of opposites like 'this is done, this is not done'?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.12 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Where is dharma, where is pleasure, where is wealth, where is discernment, for the yogi free of opposites like 'this is done, this is not done'?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: कृत्यं किमपि नैवास्ति न कापि हृदि रञ्जना । यथा जीवनमेवेह जीवन्मुक्तस्य योगिनः ॥
verses.iast: kṛtyaṃ kimapi naivāsti na kāpi hṛdi rañjanā | yathā jīvanameveha jīvanmuktasya yoginaḥ ||
verses.en: The yogi free while living has no duty left to do and no attachment in his heart. He lives as life comes.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.13 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The yogi free while living has no duty left to do and no attachment in his heart. He lives as life comes."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: क्व मोहः क्व च वा विश्वं क्व तद् ध्यानं क्व मुक्तता । सर्वसङ्कल्पसीमायां विश्रान्तस्य महात्मनः ॥
verses.iast: kva mohaḥ kva ca vā viśvaṃ kva tad dhyānaṃ kva muktatā | sarvasaṅkalpasīmāyāṃ viśrāntasya mahātmanaḥ ||
verses.en: Where is delusion, where is the world, where is meditation on That, where is freedom, for the great soul at rest past the edge of every intention?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.14 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Where is delusion, where is the world, where is meditation on That, where is freedom, for the great soul at rest past the edge of every intention?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: येन विश्वमिदं दृष्टं स नास्तीति करोतु वै । निर्वासनः किं कुरुते पश्यन्नपि न पश्यति ॥
verses.iast: yena viśvamidaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ sa nāstīti karotu vai | nirvāsanaḥ kiṃ kurute paśyannapi na paśyati ||
verses.en: One who has seen the world may try to deny it. But what does one without tendencies have to do? Seeing, he does not see.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.15 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "One who has seen the world may try to deny it. But what does one without tendencies have to do? Seeing, he does not see."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: येन दृष्टं परं ब्रह्म सोऽहं ब्रह्मेति चिन्तयेत् । किं चिन्तयति निश्चिन्तो द्वितीयं यो न पश्यति ॥
verses.iast: yena dṛṣṭaṃ paraṃ brahma so'haṃ brahmeti cintayet | kiṃ cintayati niścinto dvitīyaṃ yo na paśyati ||
verses.en: One who has seen the supreme Brahman may think 'I am Brahman'. But what is left to think for one beyond thought, who sees no second?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.16 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "One who has seen the supreme Brahman may think 'I am Brahman'. But what is left to think for one beyond thought, who sees no second?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: दृष्टो येनात्मविक्षेपो निरोधं कुरुते त्वसौ । उदारस्तु न विक्षिप्तः साध्याभावात्करोति किम् ॥
verses.iast: dṛṣṭo yenātmavikṣepo nirodhaṃ kurute tvasau | udārastu na vikṣiptaḥ sādhyābhāvātkaroti kim ||
verses.en: One who has seen distraction in himself may work to stop it. The noble one is not distracted. With nothing to achieve, what would he do?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.17 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "One who has seen distraction in himself may work to stop it. The noble one is not distracted. With nothing to achieve, what would he do?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: धीरो लोकविपर्यस्तो वर्तमानोऽपि लोकवत् । न समाधिं न विक्षेपं न लोपं स्वस्य पश्यति ॥
verses.iast: dhīro lokaviparyasto vartamāno'pi lokavat | na samādhiṃ na vikṣepaṃ na lopaṃ svasya paśyati ||
verses.en: The steady one lives like other people and yet is unlike them. He sees no samadhi in himself, no distraction and no flaw.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.18 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The steady one lives like other people and yet is unlike them. He sees no samadhi in himself, no distraction and no flaw."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: भावाभावविहीनो यस्तृप्तो निर्वासनो बुधः । नैव किञ्चित्कृतं तेन लोकदृष्ट्या विकुर्वता ॥
verses.iast: bhāvābhāvavihīno yastṛpto nirvāsano budhaḥ | naiva kiñcitkṛtaṃ tena lokadṛṣṭyā vikurvatā ||
verses.en: The wise one, beyond being and not-being, content and free of tendencies, does nothing at all, though in other people's eyes he acts.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.19 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The wise one, beyond being and not-being, content and free of tendencies, does nothing at all, though in other people's eyes he acts."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: प्रवृत्तौ वा निवृत्तौ वा नैव धीरस्य दुर्ग्रहः । यदा यत्कर्तुमायाति तत्कृत्वा तिष्ठतः सुखम् ॥
verses.iast: pravṛttau vā nivṛttau vā naiva dhīrasya durgrahaḥ | yadā yatkartumāyāti tatkṛtvā tiṣṭhataḥ sukham ||
verses.en: The steady one does not insist on acting or on holding back. He does whatever comes to be done and stays at ease.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.20 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The steady one does not insist on acting or on holding back. He does whatever comes to be done and stays at ease."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: निर्वासनो निरालम्बः स्वच्छन्दो मुक्तबन्धनः । क्षिप्तः संस्कारवातेन चेष्टते शुष्कपर्णवत् ॥
verses.iast: nirvāsano nirālambaḥ svacchando muktabandhanaḥ | kṣiptaḥ saṃskāravātena ceṣṭate śuṣkaparṇavat ||
verses.en: Free of tendencies, leaning on nothing, moving freely, his ties undone, he is blown about by the wind of past impressions like a dry leaf.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.21 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Free of tendencies, leaning on nothing, moving freely, his ties undone, he is blown about by the wind of past impressions like a dry leaf."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: असंसारस्य तु क्वापि न हर्षो न विषादता । स शीतलमना नित्यं विदेह इव राजये ॥
verses.iast: asaṃsārasya tu kvāpi na harṣo na viṣādatā | sa śītalamanā nityaṃ videha iva rājaye ||
verses.en: One who is out of the round of the world has no joy and no gloom anywhere. With a mind always cool, he shines like one without a body.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.22 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "One who is out of the round of the world has no joy and no gloom anywhere. With a mind always cool, he shines like one without a body."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: कुत्रापि न जिहासास्ति नाशो वापि न कुत्रचित् । आत्मारामस्य धीरस्य शीतलाच्छतरात्मनः ॥
verses.iast: kutrāpi na jihāsāsti nāśo vāpi na kutracit | ātmārāmasya dhīrasya śītalācchatarātmanaḥ ||
verses.en: The steady one who delights in the Self, cool and clear inside, has no wish to give anything up and feels no loss anywhere.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.23 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The steady one who delights in the Self, cool and clear inside, has no wish to give anything up and feels no loss anywhere."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: प्रकृत्या शून्यचित्तस्य कुर्वतोऽस्य यदृच्छया । प्राकृतस्येव धीरस्य न मानो नावमानता ॥
verses.iast: prakṛtyā śūnyacittasya kurvato'sya yadṛcchayā | prākṛtasyeva dhīrasya na māno nāvamānatā ||
verses.en: His mind is empty by nature and he acts as things come. Honour and dishonour do not reach the steady one the way they reach other people.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.24 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "His mind is empty by nature and he acts as things come. Honour and dishonour do not reach the steady one the way they reach other people."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: कृतं देहेन कर्मेदं न मया शुद्धरूपिणा । इति चिन्तानुरोधी यः कुर्वन्नपि करोति न ॥
verses.iast: kṛtaṃ dehena karmedaṃ na mayā śuddharūpiṇā | iti cintānurodhī yaḥ kurvannapi karoti na ||
verses.en: 'This act was done by the body, not by me, the pure Self': one who holds to this thought does not act even while acting.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.25 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "'This act was done by the body, not by me, the pure Self': one who holds to this thought does not act even while acting."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: अतद्वादीव कुरुते न भवेदपि बालिशः । जीवन्मुक्तः सुखी श्रीमान् संसरन्नपि शोभते ॥
verses.iast: atadvādīva kurute na bhavedapi bāliśaḥ | jīvanmuktaḥ sukhī śrīmān saṃsarannapi śobhate ||
verses.en: He acts without announcing it, yet he is no fool. Free while living, happy and graced, he shines even while living a worldly life.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.26 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "He acts without announcing it, yet he is no fool. Free while living, happy and graced, he shines even while living a worldly life."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: नानाविचारसुश्रान्तो धीरो विश्रान्तिमागतः । न कल्पते न जाति न शृणोति न पश्यति ॥
verses.iast: nānāvicārasuśrānto dhīro viśrāntimāgataḥ | na kalpate na jāti na śṛṇoti na paśyati ||
verses.en: Worn out by endless reasoning, the steady one has come to rest. He does not imagine, does not know, does not hear, does not see.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.27 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Worn out by endless reasoning, the steady one has come to rest. He does not imagine, does not know, does not hear, does not see."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: असमाधेरविक्षेपान् न मुमुक्षुर्न चेतरः । निश्चित्य कल्पितं पश्यन् ब्रह्मैवास्ते महाशयः ॥
verses.iast: asamādheravikṣepān na mumukṣurna cetaraḥ | niścitya kalpitaṃ paśyan brahmaivāste mahāśayaḥ ||
verses.en: With no samadhi and no distraction, he is neither one who wants freedom nor anything else. Having seen that all is imagined, the great soul lives as Brahman itself.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.28 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "With no samadhi and no distraction, he is neither one who wants freedom nor anything else. Having seen that all is imagined, the great soul lives as Brahman itself."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: यस्यान्तः स्यादहङ्कारो न करोति करोति सः । निरहङ्कारधीरेण न किञ्चिदकृतं कृतम् ॥
verses.iast: yasyāntaḥ syādahaṅkāro na karoti karoti saḥ | nirahaṅkāradhīreṇa na kiñcidakṛtaṃ kṛtam ||
verses.en: One who has the sense of 'I' inside acts even when he does nothing. The steady one free of 'I' does nothing, even when things are done.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.29 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "One who has the sense of 'I' inside acts even when he does nothing. The steady one free of 'I' does nothing, even when things are done."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: नोद्विग्नं न च सन्तुष्टमकर्तृ स्पन्दवर्जितम् । निराशं गतसन्देहं चित्तं मुक्तस्य राजते ॥
verses.iast: nodvignaṃ na ca santuṣṭamakartṛ spandavarjitam | nirāśaṃ gatasandehaṃ cittaṃ muktasya rājate ||
verses.en: The mind of the free one shines: not upset, not pleased, not the doer, without motion, without hope, without doubt.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.30 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The mind of the free one shines: not upset, not pleased, not the doer, without motion, without hope, without doubt."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: निर्ध्यातुं चेष्टितुं वापि यच्चित्तं न प्रवर्तते । निर्निमित्तमिदं किन्तु निर्ध्यायेति विचेष्टते ॥
verses.iast: nirdhyātuṃ ceṣṭituṃ vāpi yaccittaṃ na pravartate | nirnimittamidaṃ kintu nirdhyāyeti viceṣṭate ||
verses.en: The free one's mind does not set out to meditate or to act. It meditates and acts without a reason.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.31 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The free one's mind does not set out to meditate or to act. It meditates and acts without a reason."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: तत्त्वं यथार्थमाकर्ण्य मन्दः प्राप्नोति मूढताम् । अथवा याति सङ्कोचममूढः कोऽपि मूढवत् ॥
verses.iast: tattvaṃ yathārthamākarṇya mandaḥ prāpnoti mūḍhatām | athavā yāti saṅkocamamūḍhaḥ ko'pi mūḍhavat ||
verses.en: Hearing the truth as it is, a dull person is bewildered. A sharp one turns inward and may look like a dull one.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.32 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Hearing the truth as it is, a dull person is bewildered. A sharp one turns inward and may look like a dull one."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: एकाग्रता निरोधो वा मूढैरभ्यस्यते भृशम् । धीराः कृत्यं न पश्यन्ति सुप्तवत्स्वपदे स्थिताः ॥
verses.iast: ekāgratā nirodho vā mūḍhairabhyasyate bhṛśam | dhīrāḥ kṛtyaṃ na paśyanti suptavatsvapade sthitāḥ ||
verses.en: The confused work hard at concentration and control. The steady see nothing to do. They rest in their own state like people asleep.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.33 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The confused work hard at concentration and control. The steady see nothing to do. They rest in their own state like people asleep."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: अप्रयत्नात् प्रयत्नाद् वा मूढो नाप्नोति निर्वृतिम् । तत्त्वनिश्चयमात्रेण प्राज्ञो भवति निर्वृतः ॥
verses.iast: aprayatnāt prayatnād vā mūḍho nāpnoti nirvṛtim | tattvaniścayamātreṇa prājño bhavati nirvṛtaḥ ||
verses.en: With effort or without it, the confused do not find rest. The wise are at rest just by being sure of the truth.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.34 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "With effort or without it, the confused do not find rest. The wise are at rest just by being sure of the truth."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: शुद्धं बुद्धं प्रियं पूर्णं निष्प्रपञ्चं निरामयम् । आत्मानं तं न जानन्ति तत्राभ्यासपरा जनाः ॥
verses.iast: śuddhaṃ buddhaṃ priyaṃ pūrṇaṃ niṣprapañcaṃ nirāmayam | ātmānaṃ taṃ na jānanti tatrābhyāsaparā janāḥ ||
verses.en: People devoted to practice do not know the Self: pure, awake, dear, whole, beyond the spread of the world, untouched by sorrow.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.35 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "People devoted to practice do not know the Self: pure, awake, dear, whole, beyond the spread of the world, untouched by sorrow."
verses.notice: Six qualities of the Self are listed, and then the surprise: those devoted to practice do not know it.

words.m: beyond the spread of the world

verses.commentary: The first line is a portrait of the Self in six words. Pure, awake, dear, whole, beyond the spread of the world, free of sickness. Priya, dear, is a striking choice. The Upanishads say that everything is loved for the sake of the Self, and here the Self itself is called the beloved. Then the second line turns: people devoted to practice do not know it. This is the same point made in 1.15 and repeated through chapter 18. If you practise in order to reach the Self, you have placed it somewhere else, at the end of the practice. Advaita teachers read the verse as aimed at a particular trap, where years of discipline become a way of postponing recognition. They do not read it as a ban on practice for everyone. The Bhagavad Gita takes a different emphasis and tells Arjuna that the restless mind is steadied by practice and dispassion. Many readers find both true at different stages. People searching for 'Ashtavakra samhita 18.35' are looking for this verse.

bridge.note: Krishna tells Arjuna the restless mind is steadied by practice and dispassion, the step Ashtavakra treats as already behind his student.

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: नाप्नोति कर्मणा मोक्षं विमूढोऽभ्यासरूपिणा । धन्यो विज्ञानमात्रेण मुक्तस्तिष्ठत्यविक्रियः ॥
verses.iast: nāpnoti karmaṇā mokṣaṃ vimūḍho'bhyāsarūpiṇā | dhanyo vijñānamātreṇa muktastiṣṭhatyavikriyaḥ ||
verses.en: The confused person does not gain freedom by repeated action, which is all practice is. The fortunate one, by knowing alone, stands free and unchanging.

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: मूढो नाप्नोति तद् ब्रह्म यतो भवितुमिच्छति । अनिच्छन्नपि धीरो हि परब्रह्मस्वरूपभाक् ॥
verses.iast: mūḍho nāpnoti tad brahma yato bhavitumicchati | anicchannapi dhīro hi parabrahmasvarūpabhāk ||
verses.en: The confused do not reach Brahman because they want to become it. The steady one, without even wanting it, has the nature of the supreme Brahman.

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: निराधारा ग्रहव्यग्रा मूढाः संसारपोषकाः । एतस्यानर्थमूलस्य मूलच्छेदः कृतो बुधैः ॥
verses.iast: nirādhārā grahavyagrā mūḍhāḥ saṃsārapoṣakāḥ | etasyānarthamūlasya mūlacchedaḥ kṛto budhaiḥ ||
verses.en: With no ground to stand on and restless to grasp, the confused keep the world going. The wise cut the root of this root of trouble.

verses.sa: न शान्तिं लभते मूढो यतः शमितुमिच्छति । धीरस्तत्त्वं विनिश्चित्य सर्वदा शान्तमानसः ॥
verses.iast: na śāntiṃ labhate mūḍho yataḥ śamitumicchati | dhīrastattvaṃ viniścitya sarvadā śāntamānasaḥ ||
verses.en: The confused one does not find peace because he is trying to make himself peaceful. The steady one, sure of the truth, is always calm.

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: क्वात्मनो दर्शनं तस्य यद् दृष्टमवलम्बते । धीरास्तं तं न पश्यन्ति पश्यन्त्यात्मानमव्ययम् ॥
verses.iast: kvātmano darśanaṃ tasya yad dṛṣṭamavalambate | dhīrāstaṃ taṃ na paśyanti paśyantyātmānamavyayam ||
verses.en: How can one who leans on what is seen see the Self? The steady do not see this and that. They see the Self that does not change.

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: क्व निरोधो विमूढस्य यो निर्बन्धं करोति वै । स्वारामस्यैव धीरस्य सर्वदासावकृत्रिमः ॥
verses.iast: kva nirodho vimūḍhasya yo nirbandhaṃ karoti vai | svārāmasyaiva dhīrasya sarvadāsāvakṛtrimaḥ ||
verses.en: Where is control of the mind for the confused one who forces it? For the steady one who delights in the Self, it comes naturally, always.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.41 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: भावस्य भावकः कश्चिन् न किञ्चिद् भावकोपरः । उभयाभावकः कश्चिद् एवमेव निराकुलः ॥
verses.iast: bhāvasya bhāvakaḥ kaścin na kiñcid bhāvakoparaḥ | ubhayābhāvakaḥ kaścid evameva nirākulaḥ ||
verses.en: One person thinks things exist. Another thinks nothing exists. Rare is the one who thinks neither, and so stays undisturbed.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.42 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "One person thinks things exist. Another thinks nothing exists. Rare is the one who thinks neither, and so stays undisturbed."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: शुद्धमद्वयमात्मानं भावयन्ति कुबुद्धयः । न तु जानन्ति संमोहाद्यावज्जीवमनिर्वृताः ॥
verses.iast: śuddhamadvayamātmānaṃ bhāvayanti kubuddhayaḥ | na tu jānanti saṃmohādyāvajjīvamanirvṛtāḥ ||
verses.en: The dull-minded meditate on the Self as pure and one, but through confusion they do not know it, and stay unsatisfied all their lives.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.43 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: मुमुक्षोर्बुद्धिरालम्बमन्तरेण न विद्यते । निरालम्बैव निष्कामा बुद्धिर्मुक्तस्य सर्वदा ॥
verses.iast: mumukṣorbuddhirālambamantareṇa na vidyate | nirālambaiva niṣkāmā buddhirmuktasya sarvadā ||
verses.en: The mind of one who wants freedom needs something to lean on. The mind of the free one leans on nothing and wants nothing, always.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.44 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The mind of one who wants freedom needs something to lean on. The mind of the free one leans on nothing and wants nothing, always."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: विषयद्वीपिनो वीक्ष्य चकिताः शरणार्थिनः । विशन्ति झटिति क्रोडं निरोधैकाग्रसिद्धये ॥
verses.iast: viṣayadvīpino vīkṣya cakitāḥ śaraṇārthinaḥ | viśanti jhaṭiti kroḍaṃ nirodhaikāgrasiddhaye ||
verses.en: Seeing the tigers of the senses' objects, frightened people looking for shelter rush into a cave to gain control and focus.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.45 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Seeing the tigers of the senses' objects, frightened people looking for shelter rush into a cave to gain control and focus."

verses.iast: nirvāsanaṃ hariṃ dṛṣṭvā tūṣṇīṃ viṣayadantinaḥ | palāyante na śaktāste sevante kṛtacāṭavaḥ ||
verses.en: Seeing the lion without tendencies, the elephants of the senses' objects run off without a sound, or, if they cannot, stay and serve him like flatterers.

verses.en: Free of doubt, his mind joined to the Self, he does not take up practices for freedom. Seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, he lives at ease.

verses.en: Clear-minded and settled just by hearing the truth, he does not look on right conduct, wrong conduct or indifference as his concern.

verses.en: Whatever comes to be done, the straightforward one does it, good or bad. His actions are like a child's.

verses.iast: svātantryātsukhamāpnoti svātantryāllabhate param | svātantryānnirvṛtiṃ gacchetsvātantryāt paramaṃ padam ||
verses.en: Through inner freedom one finds happiness. Through inner freedom one reaches the highest. Through inner freedom one comes to rest. Through inner freedom, the supreme state.

verses.en: When one sees the Self as neither doer nor enjoyer, all the movements of the mind wear away.

verses.sa: उच्छृङ्खलाप्यकृतिका स्थितिर्धीरस्य राजते । न तु सस्पृहचित्तस्य शान्तिर्मूढस्य कृत्रिमा ॥
verses.iast: ucchṛṅkhalāpyakṛtikā sthitirdhīrasya rājate | na tu saspṛhacittasya śāntirmūḍhasya kṛtrimā ||
verses.en: The steady one's way of living shines, unbound and unforced. The forced calm of the confused, whose mind still wants, does not shine.

verses.sa: विलसन्ति महाभोगैर्विशन्ति गिरिगह्वरान् । निरस्तकल्पना धीरा अबद्धा मुक्तबुद्धयः ॥
verses.iast: vilasanti mahābhogairviśanti girigahvarān | nirastakalpanā dhīrā abaddhā muktabuddhayaḥ ||
verses.en: Steady ones, free of imagining, unbound, their minds set free, sometimes enjoy great pleasures and sometimes go into mountain caves.

verses.sa: श्रोत्रियं देवतां तीर्थमङ्गनां भूपतिं प्रियम् । दृष्ट्वा सम्पूज्य धीरस्य न कापि हृदि वासना ॥
verses.iast: śrotriyaṃ devatāṃ tīrthamaṅganāṃ bhūpatiṃ priyam | dṛṣṭvā sampūjya dhīrasya na kāpi hṛdi vāsanā ||
verses.en: When the steady one sees and honours a scholar of the Vedas, a deity, a holy place, a woman, a king or a loved one, no desire stirs in his heart.

verses.sa: भृत्यैः पुत्रैः कलत्रैश्च दौहित्रैश्चापि गोत्रजैः । विहस्य धिक्कृतो योगी न याति विकृतिं मनाक् ॥

verses.sa: सन्तुष्टोऽपि न सन्तुष्टः खिन्नोऽपि न च खिद्यते । तस्याश्चर्यदशां तां तां तादृशा एव जानते ॥
verses.iast: santuṣṭo'pi na santuṣṭaḥ khinno'pi na ca khidyate | tasyāścaryadaśāṃ tāṃ tāṃ tādṛśā eva jānate ||
verses.en: Pleased, he is not pleased. Pained, he is not pained. Only those like him know such wondrous states.

verses.sa: कर्तव्यतैव संसारो न तां पश्यन्ति सूरयः । शून्याकारा निराकारा निर्विकारा निरामयाः ॥
verses.iast: kartavyataiva saṃsāro na tāṃ paśyanti sūrayaḥ | śūnyākārā nirākārā nirvikārā nirāmayāḥ ||
verses.en: Having duties is the world itself. The wise do not see it. They are empty of shape, without form, unchanging, untouched by pain.
