verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: अकुर्वन्नपि सङ्क्षोभाद् व्यग्रः सर्वत्र मूढधीः । कुर्वन्नपि तु कृत्यानि कुशलो हि निराकुलः ॥
verses.iast: akurvannapi saṅkṣobhād vyagraḥ sarvatra mūḍhadhīḥ | kurvannapi tu kṛtyāni kuśalo hi nirākulaḥ ||
verses.en: The confused one, even doing nothing, is agitated and restless everywhere. The able one, even doing his work, stays undisturbed.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.58 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The confused one, even doing nothing, is agitated and restless everywhere. The able one, even doing his work, stays undisturbed."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: सुखमास्ते सुखं शेते सुखमायाति याति च । सुखं वक्ति सुखं भुङ्क्ते व्यवहारेऽपि शान्तधीः ॥
verses.iast: sukhamāste sukhaṃ śete sukhamāyāti yāti ca | sukhaṃ vakti sukhaṃ bhuṅkte vyavahāre'pi śāntadhīḥ ||
verses.en: At ease he sits, at ease he sleeps, at ease he comes and goes, at ease he speaks, at ease he eats. Calm-minded, he is at ease even in daily dealings.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.59 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "At ease he sits, at ease he sleeps, at ease he comes and goes, at ease he speaks, at ease he eats. Calm-minded, he is at ease even in daily dealings."
verses.notice: The word sukham, at ease, appears six times in two lines.
verses.commentary: After many verses of paradox and negation, chapter 18 offers this picture of ordinary life. At ease he sits, at ease he sleeps, at ease he comes and goes, at ease he speaks, at ease he eats. The word sukham opens each phrase, and the repetition is the meaning: the same ease runs through every activity. The last phrase is vyavahāre 'pi, even in vyavahāra, which means business, transactions, the give and take of daily life. The calm-minded person needs no quiet cave. He stays calm while paying bills and talking to neighbours. The Advaita reading treats this as the mark of a jīvanmukta, one free while living. Freedom shows itself in how a person eats lunch and answers questions. A reader can use the verse as a check during an ordinary day. Sitting, walking, speaking, eating: is there ease in it? The verse does not ask for different activities, only for a different quality in the same ones.

bridge.note: Krishna says the one who knows the truth thinks 'I do nothing' while seeing, hearing, walking, sleeping and breathing.

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: स्वभावाद्यस्य नैवार्तिर्लोकवद् व्यवहारिणः । महाहृद इवाक्षोभ्यो गतक्लेशः सुशोभते ॥
verses.iast: svabhāvādyasya naivārtirlokavad vyavahāriṇaḥ | mahāhṛda ivākṣobhyo gatakleśaḥ suśobhate ||
verses.en: One who by nature feels no distress while dealing with the world like anyone else shines free of trouble, unstirred like a great lake.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.60 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "One who by nature feels no distress while dealing with the world like anyone else shines free of trouble, unstirred like a great lake."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: निवृत्तिरपि मूढस्य प्रवृत्ति रुपजायते । प्रवृत्तिरपि धीरस्य निवृत्तिफलभागिनी ॥
verses.iast: nivṛttirapi mūḍhasya pravṛtti rupajāyate | pravṛttirapi dhīrasya nivṛttiphalabhāginī ||
verses.en: Even the confused person's holding back becomes a kind of action. Even the steady one's action bears the fruit of holding back.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.61 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Even the confused person's holding back becomes a kind of action. Even the steady one's action bears the fruit of holding back."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: परिग्रहेषु वैराग्यं प्रायो मूढस्य दृश्यते । देहे विगलिताशस्य क्व रागः क्व विरागता ॥
verses.iast: parigraheṣu vairāgyaṃ prāyo mūḍhasya dṛśyate | dehe vigalitāśasya kva rāgaḥ kva virāgatā ||
verses.en: The confused often show dispassion toward their possessions. For one whose clinging to the body has melted, where is attachment, and where is dispassion?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.62 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The confused often show dispassion toward their possessions. For one whose clinging to the body has melted, where is attachment, and where is dispassion?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: भावनाभावनासक्ता दृष्टिर्मूढस्य सर्वदा । भाव्यभावनया सा तु स्वस्थस्यादृष्टिरूपिणी ॥
verses.iast: bhāvanābhāvanāsaktā dṛṣṭirmūḍhasya sarvadā | bhāvyabhāvanayā sā tu svasthasyādṛṣṭirūpiṇī ||
verses.en: The confused person's gaze is always caught up in thinking and not thinking. For one at rest in himself, even thinking about something is a way of not seeing it.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.63 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The confused person's gaze is always caught up in thinking and not thinking. For one at rest in himself, even thinking about something is a way of not seeing it."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: सर्वारम्भेषु निष्कामो यश्चरेद् बालवन् मुनिः । न लेपस्तस्य शुद्धस्य क्रियमाणेऽपि कर्मणि ॥
verses.iast: sarvārambheṣu niṣkāmo yaścared bālavan muniḥ | na lepastasya śuddhasya kriyamāṇe'pi karmaṇi ||
verses.en: The sage who acts like a child, without desire in anything he begins, is pure, and is not stained even by the work he does.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.64 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The sage who acts like a child, without desire in anything he begins, is pure, and is not stained even by the work he does."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: स एव धन्य आत्मज्ञः सर्वभावेषु यः समः । पश्यन् शृण्वन् स्पृशन् जिघ्रन्अश्नन्निस्तर्षमानसः ॥
verses.iast: sa eva dhanya ātmajñaḥ sarvabhāveṣu yaḥ samaḥ | paśyan śṛṇvan spṛśan jighranaśnannistarṣamānasaḥ ||
verses.en: Blessed is the one who knows the Self and stays the same in every state: seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, with a mind free of thirst.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.65 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Blessed is the one who knows the Self and stays the same in every state: seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, with a mind free of thirst."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: क्व संसारः क्व चाभासः क्व साध्यं क्व च साधनम् । आकाशस्येव धीरस्य निर्विकल्पस्य सर्वदा ॥
verses.iast: kva saṃsāraḥ kva cābhāsaḥ kva sādhyaṃ kva ca sādhanam | ākāśasyeva dhīrasya nirvikalpasya sarvadā ||
verses.en: Where is the world, where is its appearance, where is the goal and where the means, for the steady one who is always like the sky, free of wavering thought?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.66 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Where is the world, where is its appearance, where is the goal and where the means, for the steady one who is always like the sky, free of wavering thought?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: स जयत्यर्थसंन्यासी पूर्णस्वरसविग्रहः । अकृत्रिमोऽनवच्छिन्ने समाधिर्यस्य वर्तते ॥
verses.iast: sa jayatyarthasaṃnyāsī pūrṇasvarasavigrahaḥ | akṛtrimo'navacchinne samādhiryasya vartate ||
verses.en: Victorious is the one who has left all aims, who is the form of complete joy, and whose natural samadhi goes on unbroken.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.67 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Victorious is the one who has left all aims, who is the form of complete joy, and whose natural samadhi goes on unbroken."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: बहुनात्र किमुक्तेन ज्ञाततत्त्वो महाशयः । भोगमोक्षनिराकाङ्क्षी सदा सर्वत्र नीरसः ॥
verses.iast: bahunātra kimuktena jñātatattvo mahāśayaḥ | bhogamokṣanirākāṅkṣī sadā sarvatra nīrasaḥ ||
verses.en: What more is there to say? The great soul who knows the truth wants neither enjoyment nor freedom, and has no taste for anything, always, everywhere.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.68 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "What more is there to say? The great soul who knows the truth wants neither enjoyment nor freedom, and has no taste for anything, always, everywhere."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: महदादि जगद्द्वैतं नाममात्रविजृम्भितम् । विहाय शुद्धबोधस्य किं कृत्यमवशिष्यते ॥
verses.iast: mahadādi jagaddvaitaṃ nāmamātravijṛmbhitam | vihāya śuddhabodhasya kiṃ kṛtyamavaśiṣyate ||
verses.en: The duality of the world, beginning with the great principle of nature, is only names spreading out. Having dropped it, what is left to do for one who is pure awareness?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.69 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The duality of the world, beginning with the great principle of nature, is only names spreading out. Having dropped it, what is left to do for one who is pure awareness?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: भ्रमभूतमिदं सर्वं किञ्चिन्नास्तीति निश्चयी । अलक्ष्यस्फुरणः शुद्धः स्वभावेनैव शाम्यति ॥
verses.iast: bhramabhūtamidaṃ sarvaṃ kiñcinnāstīti niścayī | alakṣyasphuraṇaḥ śuddhaḥ svabhāvenaiva śāmyati ||
verses.en: Certain that all this is born of error and nothing is, the pure one, whose shining nobody can see, comes to rest by his own nature.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.70 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Certain that all this is born of error and nothing is, the pure one, whose shining nobody can see, comes to rest by his own nature."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: शुद्धस्फुरणरूपस्य दृश्यभावमपश्यतः । क्व विधिः क्व च वैराग्यं क्व त्यागः क्व शमोऽपि वा ॥
verses.iast: śuddhasphuraṇarūpasya dṛśyabhāvamapaśyataḥ | kva vidhiḥ kva ca vairāgyaṃ kva tyāgaḥ kva śamo'pi vā ||
verses.en: For one whose form is pure shining, who does not see objects as real, where is rule, where is dispassion, where is giving up, where is calm?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.71 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "For one whose form is pure shining, who does not see objects as real, where is rule, where is dispassion, where is giving up, where is calm?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: स्फुरतोऽनन्तरूपेण प्रकृतिं च न पश्यतः । क्व बन्धः क्व च वा मोक्षः क्व हर्षः क्व विषादिता ॥
verses.iast: sphurato'nantarūpeṇa prakṛtiṃ ca na paśyataḥ | kva bandhaḥ kva ca vā mokṣaḥ kva harṣaḥ kva viṣāditā ||
verses.en: For one who shines as the endless and does not see nature apart from himself, where is bondage, where is freedom, where is joy, where is grief?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.72 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "For one who shines as the endless and does not see nature apart from himself, where is bondage, where is freedom, where is joy, where is grief?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: बुद्धिपर्यन्तसंसारे मायामात्रं विवर्तते । निर्ममो निरहङ्कारो निष्कामः शोभते बुधः ॥
verses.iast: buddhiparyantasaṃsāre māyāmātraṃ vivartate | nirmamo nirahaṅkāro niṣkāmaḥ śobhate budhaḥ ||
verses.en: In this world, which lasts as long as the intellect does, only illusion turns. The wise one, without 'mine', without 'I', without desire, shines.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.73 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "In this world, which lasts as long as the intellect does, only illusion turns. The wise one, without 'mine', without 'I', without desire, shines."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: अक्षयं गतसन्तापमात्मानं पश्यतो मुनेः । क्व विद्या च क्व वा विश्वं क्व देहोऽहं ममेति वा ॥
verses.iast: akṣayaṃ gatasantāpamātmānaṃ paśyato muneḥ | kva vidyā ca kva vā viśvaṃ kva deho'haṃ mameti vā ||
verses.en: For the sage who sees the Self as imperishable and free of pain, where is knowledge, where is the world, where is 'I am the body' or 'this is mine'?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.74 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "For the sage who sees the Self as imperishable and free of pain, where is knowledge, where is the world, where is 'I am the body' or 'this is mine'?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: निरोधादीनि कर्माणि जहाति जडधीर्यदि । मनोरथान् प्रलापांश्च कर्तुमाप्नोत्यतत्क्षणात् ॥
verses.iast: nirodhādīni karmāṇi jahāti jaḍadhīryadi | manorathān pralāpāṃśca kartumāpnotyatatkṣaṇāt ||
verses.en: If a dull-minded person drops practices like control of the mind, he at once starts on daydreams and chatter.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.75 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "If a dull-minded person drops practices like control of the mind, he at once starts on daydreams and chatter."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: मन्दः श्रुत्वापि तद्वस्तु न जहाति विमूढताम् । निर्विकल्पो बहिर्यत्नादन्तर्विषयलालसः ॥
verses.iast: mandaḥ śrutvāpi tadvastu na jahāti vimūḍhatām | nirvikalpo bahiryatnādantarviṣayalālasaḥ ||
verses.en: Even after hearing the truth, the dull one does not give up his confusion. He looks free of thought through outward effort, but inside he still longs for objects.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.76 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Even after hearing the truth, the dull one does not give up his confusion. He looks free of thought through outward effort, but inside he still longs for objects."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: ज्ञानाद् गलितकर्मा यो लोकदृष्ट्यापि कर्मकृत् । नाप्नोत्यवसरं कर्त्रुं वक्तुमेव न किञ्चन ॥
verses.iast: jñānād galitakarmā yo lokadṛṣṭyāpi karmakṛt | nāpnotyavasaraṃ kartruṃ vaktumeva na kiñcana ||
verses.en: One whose actions have fallen away through knowledge, though others see him act, finds no occasion to do or say anything.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.77 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "One whose actions have fallen away through knowledge, though others see him act, finds no occasion to do or say anything."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: क्व तमः क्व प्रकाशो वा हानं क्व च न किञ्चन । निर्विकारस्य धीरस्य निरातङ्कस्य सर्वदा ॥
verses.iast: kva tamaḥ kva prakāśo vā hānaṃ kva ca na kiñcana | nirvikārasya dhīrasya nirātaṅkasya sarvadā ||
verses.en: Where is darkness, where is light, where is loss, for the steady one who is always unchanging and fearless? There is nothing.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.78 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Where is darkness, where is light, where is loss, for the steady one who is always unchanging and fearless? There is nothing."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: क्व धैर्यं क्व विवेकित्वं क्व निरातङ्कतापि वा । अनिर्वाच्यस्वभावस्य निःस्वभावस्य योगिनः ॥
verses.iast: kva dhairyaṃ kva vivekitvaṃ kva nirātaṅkatāpi vā | anirvācyasvabhāvasya niḥsvabhāvasya yoginaḥ ||
verses.en: Where is patience, where is discernment, where is even fearlessness, for the yogi whose nature cannot be described and who has no separate nature?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.79 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Where is patience, where is discernment, where is even fearlessness, for the yogi whose nature cannot be described and who has no separate nature?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: न स्वर्गो नैव नरको जीवन्मुक्तिर्न चैव हि । बहुनात्र किमुक्तेन योगदृष्ट्या न किञ्चन ॥
verses.iast: na svargo naiva narako jīvanmuktirna caiva hi | bahunātra kimuktena yogadṛṣṭyā na kiñcana ||
verses.en: There is no heaven, no hell, not even freedom while living. What more is there to say? In the yogi's sight, nothing at all is.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.80 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "There is no heaven, no hell, not even freedom while living. What more is there to say? In the yogi's sight, nothing at all is."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: नैव प्रार्थयते लाभं नालाभेनानुशोचति । धीरस्य शीतलं चित्तममृतेनैव पूरितम् ॥
verses.iast: naiva prārthayate lābhaṃ nālābhenānuśocati | dhīrasya śītalaṃ cittamamṛtenaiva pūritam ||
verses.en: He does not pray for gain or grieve over loss. The steady one's cool mind is filled with nectar.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.81 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "He does not pray for gain or grieve over loss. The steady one's cool mind is filled with nectar."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: न शान्तं स्तौति निष्कामो न दुष्टमपि निन्दति । समदुःखसुखस्तृप्तः किञ्चित् कृत्यं न पश्यति ॥
verses.iast: na śāntaṃ stauti niṣkāmo na duṣṭamapi nindati | samaduḥkhasukhastṛptaḥ kiñcit kṛtyaṃ na paśyati ||
verses.en: The one without desire does not praise the calm or blame the wicked. The same in sorrow and joy, content, he sees nothing he must do.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.82 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The one without desire does not praise the calm or blame the wicked. The same in sorrow and joy, content, he sees nothing he must do."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: धीरो न द्वेष्टि संसारमात्मानं न दिदृक्षति । हर्षामर्षविनिर्मुक्तो न मृतो न च जीवति ॥
verses.iast: dhīro na dveṣṭi saṃsāramātmānaṃ na didṛkṣati | harṣāmarṣavinirmukto na mṛto na ca jīvati ||
verses.en: The steady one does not hate the world or long to see the Self. Free of joy and anger, he is not dead and he is not alive.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.83 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The steady one does not hate the world or long to see the Self. Free of joy and anger, he is not dead and he is not alive."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: निःस्नेहः पुत्रदारादौ निष्कामो विषयेषु च । निश्चिन्तः स्वशरीरेऽपि निराशः शोभते बुधः ॥
verses.iast: niḥsnehaḥ putradārādau niṣkāmo viṣayeṣu ca | niścintaḥ svaśarīre'pi nirāśaḥ śobhate budhaḥ ||
verses.en: Without clinging fondness for children, wife and the rest, without desire for objects, without worry even about his own body, without expectations, the wise one shines.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.84 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Without clinging fondness for children, wife and the rest, without desire for objects, without worry even about his own body, without expectations, the wise one shines."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: तुष्टिः सर्वत्र धीरस्य यथापतितवर्तिनः । स्वच्छन्दं चरतो देशान् यत्रस्तमितशायिनः ॥
verses.iast: tuṣṭiḥ sarvatra dhīrasya yathāpatitavartinaḥ | svacchandaṃ carato deśān yatrastamitaśāyinaḥ ||
verses.en: The steady one is content everywhere, living on whatever falls his way, wandering where he likes and sleeping wherever the sun sets.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.85 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The steady one is content everywhere, living on whatever falls his way, wandering where he likes and sleeping wherever the sun sets."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: पततूदेतु वा देहो नास्य चिन्ता महात्मनः । स्वभावभूमिविश्रान्तिविस्मृताशेषसंसृतेः ॥
verses.iast: patatūdetu vā deho nāsya cintā mahātmanaḥ | svabhāvabhūmiviśrāntivismṛtāśeṣasaṃsṛteḥ ||
verses.en: Let the body fall or rise. The great soul does not think about it. Resting on the ground of his own nature, he has forgotten the whole round of birth.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.86 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Let the body fall or rise. The great soul does not think about it. Resting on the ground of his own nature, he has forgotten the whole round of birth."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: अकिञ्चनः कामचारो निर्द्वन्द्वश्छिन्नसंशयः । असक्तः सर्वभावेषु केवलो रमते बुधः ॥
verses.iast: akiñcanaḥ kāmacāro nirdvandvaśchinnasaṃśayaḥ | asaktaḥ sarvabhāveṣu kevalo ramate budhaḥ ||
verses.en: Owning nothing, moving freely, free of opposites, his doubts cut, unattached to anything, the wise one delights alone.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.87 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Owning nothing, moving freely, free of opposites, his doubts cut, unattached to anything, the wise one delights alone."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: निर्ममः शोभते धीरः समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः । सुभिन्नहृदयग्रन्थिर्विनिर्धूतरजस्तमः ॥
verses.iast: nirmamaḥ śobhate dhīraḥ samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ | subhinnahṛdayagranthirvinirdhūtarajastamaḥ ||
verses.en: Without 'mine', the steady one shines. To him a clod, a stone and gold are the same. The knots of his heart are cut, and restlessness and dullness are shaken off.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.88 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Without 'mine', the steady one shines. To him a clod, a stone and gold are the same. The knots of his heart are cut, and restlessness and dullness are shaken off."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: सर्वत्रानवधानस्य न किञ्चिद् वासना हृदि । मुक्तात्मनो वितृप्तस्य तुलना केन जायते ॥
verses.iast: sarvatrānavadhānasya na kiñcid vāsanā hṛdi | muktātmano vitṛptasya tulanā kena jāyate ||
verses.en: He pays no special heed to anything and no tendency is left in his heart. Free and wholly content, with whom can he be compared?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.89 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "He pays no special heed to anything and no tendency is left in his heart. Free and wholly content, with whom can he be compared?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: जानन्नपि न जानाति पश्यन्नपि न पश्यति । ब्रुवन्नपि न च ब्रूते कोऽन्यो निर्वासनादृते ॥
verses.iast: jānannapi na jānāti paśyannapi na paśyati | bruvannapi na ca brūte ko'nyo nirvāsanādṛte ||
verses.en: Knowing, he does not know. Seeing, he does not see. Speaking, he does not speak. Who can be like this except one without tendencies?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.90 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Knowing, he does not know. Seeing, he does not see. Speaking, he does not speak. Who can be like this except one without tendencies?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: भिक्षुर्वा भूपतिर्वापि यो निष्कामः स शोभते । भावेषु गलिता यस्य शोभनाशोभना मतिः ॥
verses.iast: bhikṣurvā bhūpatirvāpi yo niṣkāmaḥ sa śobhate | bhāveṣu galitā yasya śobhanāśobhanā matiḥ ||
verses.en: Beggar or king, the one without desire shines, he whose ideas of good and bad in things have melted away.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.91 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Beggar or king, the one without desire shines, he whose ideas of good and bad in things have melted away."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: क्व स्वाच्छन्द्यं क्व सङ्कोचः क्व वा तत्त्वविनिश्चयः । निर्व्याजार्जवभूतस्य चरितार्थस्य योगिनः ॥
verses.iast: kva svācchandyaṃ kva saṅkocaḥ kva vā tattvaviniścayaḥ | nirvyājārjavabhūtasya caritārthasya yoginaḥ ||
verses.en: Where is license, where is restraint, where is even settling the truth, for the yogi who is simplicity itself and has fulfilled his purpose?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.92 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Where is license, where is restraint, where is even settling the truth, for the yogi who is simplicity itself and has fulfilled his purpose?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: आत्मविश्रान्तितृप्तेन निराशेन गतार्तिना । अन्तर्यदनुभूयेत तत् कथं कस्य कथ्यते ॥
verses.iast: ātmaviśrāntitṛptena nirāśena gatārtinā | antaryadanubhūyeta tat kathaṃ kasya kathyate ||
verses.en: What is felt inside by one who is content resting in the Self, without hope, his sorrows gone: how can it be told, and to whom?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.93 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "What is felt inside by one who is content resting in the Self, without hope, his sorrows gone: how can it be told, and to whom?"

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: सुप्तोऽपि न सुषुप्तौ च स्वप्नेऽपि शयितो न च । जागरेऽपि न जागर्ति धीरस्तृप्तः पदे पदे ॥
verses.iast: supto'pi na suṣuptau ca svapne'pi śayito na ca | jāgare'pi na jāgarti dhīrastṛptaḥ pade pade ||
verses.en: Asleep, he is not in deep sleep. Dreaming, he is not lying down. Awake, he is not awake. The steady one is content at every step.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.94 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Asleep, he is not in deep sleep. Dreaming, he is not lying down. Awake, he is not awake. The steady one is content at every step."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: ज्ञः सचिन्तोऽपि निश्चिन्तः सेन्द्रियोऽपि निरिन्द्रियः । सुबुद्धिरपि निर्बुद्धिः साहङ्कारोऽनहङ्कृतिः ॥
verses.iast: jñaḥ sacinto'pi niścintaḥ sendriyo'pi nirindriyaḥ | subuddhirapi nirbuddhiḥ sāhaṅkāro'nahaṅkṛtiḥ ||
verses.en: The knower has thoughts and is free of thought, has senses and is beyond them, has an intellect and is beyond it, has an 'I' and is free of it.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.95 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The knower has thoughts and is free of thought, has senses and is beyond them, has an intellect and is beyond it, has an 'I' and is free of it."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: न सुखी न च वा दुःखी न विरक्तो न सङ्गवान् । न मुमुक्षुर्न वा मुक्ता न किञ्चिन्न च किञ्चन ॥
verses.iast: na sukhī na ca vā duḥkhī na virakto na saṅgavān | na mumukṣurna vā muktā na kiñcinna ca kiñcana ||
verses.en: He is not happy and not unhappy, not detached and not attached, not one who wants freedom and not one who is free. He is not something and not nothing.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.96 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "He is not happy and not unhappy, not detached and not attached, not one who wants freedom and not one who is free. He is not something and not nothing."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: विक्षेपेऽपि न विक्षिप्तः समाधौ न समाधिमान् । जाड्येऽपि न जडो धन्यः पाण्डित्येऽपि न पण्डितः ॥
verses.iast: vikṣepe'pi na vikṣiptaḥ samādhau na samādhimān | jāḍye'pi na jaḍo dhanyaḥ pāṇḍitye'pi na paṇḍitaḥ ||
verses.en: Distracted, he is not distracted. In samadhi, he is not in samadhi. In dullness, he is not dull. Learned, he is not learned. Blessed is he.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.97 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Distracted, he is not distracted. In samadhi, he is not in samadhi. In dullness, he is not dull. Learned, he is not learned. Blessed is he."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: मुक्तो यथास्थितिस्वस्थः कृतकर्तव्यनिर्वृतः । समः सर्वत्र वैतृष्ण्यान्न स्मरत्यकृतं कृतम् ॥
verses.iast: mukto yathāsthitisvasthaḥ kṛtakartavyanirvṛtaḥ | samaḥ sarvatra vaitṛṣṇyānna smaratyakṛtaṃ kṛtam ||
verses.en: The free one rests in himself in every state, at peace with what is done and what is to be done, the same everywhere. Free of thirst, he does not recall what he did or left undone.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.98 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "The free one rests in himself in every state, at peace with what is done and what is to be done, the same everywhere. Free of thirst, he does not recall what he did or left undone."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: न प्रीयते वन्द्यमानो निन्द्यमानो न कुप्यति । नैवोद्विजति मरणे जीवने नाभिनन्दति ॥
verses.iast: na prīyate vandyamāno nindyamāno na kupyati | naivodvijati maraṇe jīvane nābhinandati ||
verses.en: Praised, he is not pleased. Blamed, he is not angry. He does not shrink from death or cling to life.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.99 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "Praised, he is not pleased. Blamed, he is not angry. He does not shrink from death or cling to life."

verses.speaker: ashtavakra
verses.sa: न धावति जनाकीर्णं नारण्यमुपशान्तधीः । यथातथा यत्रतत्र सम एवावतिष्ठते ॥
verses.iast: na dhāvati janākīrṇaṃ nāraṇyamupaśāntadhīḥ | yathātathā yatratatra sama evāvatiṣṭhate ||
verses.en: A mind at peace does not run to the crowd or to the forest. As it is, wherever it is, it stays the same.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 18.100 is a verse from chapter 18 (Peace in a hundred verses). The sage Ashtavakra speaks it to King Janaka. In plain English it says: "A mind at peace does not run to the crowd or to the forest. As it is, wherever it is, it stays the same."
verses.notice: The last verse of Ashtavakra's teaching refuses both the crowd and the forest.

words.m: to the crowd, the busy town
one whose mind is at peace

verses.commentary: This is Ashtavakra's last word in the text. Chapters 19 and 20 belong to Janaka. Ashtavakra ends with a picture of where the peaceful mind lives, and the answer is nowhere in particular. It does not run to the crowded town and it does not run to the forest. Both directions were respected paths in old India. Some people sought engagement, others withdrew to hermitages. Ashtavakra declines both as escapes. Yathā tathā, however things are. Yatra tatra, wherever one is. The mind stays the same. The Advaita commentators read this as the fruit of the whole teaching. A person who knows the Self has no need to arrange circumstances, since peace does not come from them. For a reader, the verse removes a common excuse. Many of us think we would be calm somewhere else, after the move, after the project, away from the noise. Ashtavakra says the peaceful mind runs to neither. It stays where it is and is at peace there.

bridge.note: Krishna describes the one who is the same to friend and foe, in honour and dishonour, in heat and cold.

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: तत्त्वविज्ञानसन्दंशमादाय हृदयोदरात् । नानाविधपरामर्शशल्योद्धारः कृतो मया ॥
verses.iast: tattvavijñānasandaṃśamādāya hṛdayodarāt | nānāvidhaparāmarśaśalyoddhāraḥ kṛto mayā ||
verses.en: With the tongs of knowing the truth, I have pulled from deep inside my heart the thorn of many kinds of opinion.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 19.1 is a verse from chapter 19 (My own greatness). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "With the tongs of knowing the truth, I have pulled from deep inside my heart the thorn of many kinds of opinion."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: क्व धर्मः क्व च वा कामः क्व चार्थः क्व विवेकिता । क्व द्वैतं क्व च वाऽद्वैतं स्वमहिम्नि स्थितस्य मे ॥
verses.iast: kva dharmaḥ kva ca vā kāmaḥ kva cārthaḥ kva vivekitā | kva dvaitaṃ kva ca vā'dvaitaṃ svamahimni sthitasya me ||
verses.en: Where is dharma, where is pleasure, where is wealth, where is discernment, where is duality, where is even non-duality, for me who rest in my own greatness?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 19.2 is a verse from chapter 19 (My own greatness). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Where is dharma, where is pleasure, where is wealth, where is discernment, where is duality, where is even non-duality, for me who rest in my own greatness?"

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: क्व भूतं क्व भविष्यद् वा वर्तमानमपि क्व वा । क्व देशः क्व च वा नित्यं स्वमहिम्नि स्थितस्य मे ॥
verses.iast: kva bhūtaṃ kva bhaviṣyad vā vartamānamapi kva vā | kva deśaḥ kva ca vā nityaṃ svamahimni sthitasya me ||
verses.en: Where is past, where is future, where is even the present, where is place, where is even the eternal, for me who rest in my own greatness?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 19.3 is a verse from chapter 19 (My own greatness). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Where is past, where is future, where is even the present, where is place, where is even the eternal, for me who rest in my own greatness?"

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: क्व चात्मा क्व च वानात्मा क्व शुभं क्वाशुभं यथा । क्व चिन्ता क्व च वाचिन्ता स्वमहिम्नि स्थितस्य मे ॥
verses.iast: kva cātmā kva ca vānātmā kva śubhaṃ kvāśubhaṃ yathā | kva cintā kva ca vācintā svamahimni sthitasya me ||
verses.en: Where is the Self, where the not-Self, where good and bad, where worry and freedom from worry, for me who rest in my own greatness?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 19.4 is a verse from chapter 19 (My own greatness). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Where is the Self, where the not-Self, where good and bad, where worry and freedom from worry, for me who rest in my own greatness?"

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: क्व स्वप्नः क्व सुषुप्तिर्वा क्व च जागरणं तथा । क्व तुरीयं भयं वापि स्वमहिम्नि स्थितस्य मे ॥
verses.iast: kva svapnaḥ kva suṣuptirvā kva ca jāgaraṇaṃ tathā | kva turīyaṃ bhayaṃ vāpi svamahimni sthitasya me ||
verses.en: Where is dream, where is deep sleep, where is waking, where is the fourth state, where is even fear, for me who rest in my own greatness?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 19.5 is a verse from chapter 19 (My own greatness). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Where is dream, where is deep sleep, where is waking, where is the fourth state, where is even fear, for me who rest in my own greatness?"

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: क्व दूरं क्व समीपं वा बाह्यं क्वाभ्यन्तरं क्व वा । क्व स्थूलं क्व च वा सूक्ष्मं स्वमहिम्नि स्थितस्य मे ॥
verses.iast: kva dūraṃ kva samīpaṃ vā bāhyaṃ kvābhyantaraṃ kva vā | kva sthūlaṃ kva ca vā sūkṣmaṃ svamahimni sthitasya me ||
verses.en: Where is far, where is near, where is outside, where is inside, where is gross, where is subtle, for me who rest in my own greatness?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 19.6 is a verse from chapter 19 (My own greatness). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Where is far, where is near, where is outside, where is inside, where is gross, where is subtle, for me who rest in my own greatness?"

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: क्व मृत्युर्जीवितं वा क्व लोकाः क्वास्य क्व लौकिकम् । क्व लयः क्व समाधिर्वा स्वमहिम्नि स्थितस्य मे ॥
verses.iast: kva mṛtyurjīvitaṃ vā kva lokāḥ kvāsya kva laukikam | kva layaḥ kva samādhirvā svamahimni sthitasya me ||
verses.en: Where is death, where is life, where are the worlds and worldly ways, where is dissolution, where is samadhi, for me who rest in my own greatness?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 19.7 is a verse from chapter 19 (My own greatness). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Where is death, where is life, where are the worlds and worldly ways, where is dissolution, where is samadhi, for me who rest in my own greatness?"

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: अलं त्रिवर्गकथया योगस्य कथयाप्यलम् । अलं विज्ञानकथया विश्रान्तस्य ममात्मनि ॥
verses.iast: alaṃ trivargakathayā yogasya kathayāpyalam | alaṃ vijñānakathayā viśrāntasya mamātmani ||
verses.en: Enough talk of the three aims of life. Enough talk of yoga. Enough talk of knowledge too. I rest in the Self.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 19.8 is a verse from chapter 19 (My own greatness). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Enough talk of the three aims of life. Enough talk of yoga. Enough talk of knowledge too. I rest in the Self."

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: क्व भूतानि क्व देहो वा क्वेन्द्रियाणि क्व वा मनः । क्व शून्यं क्व च नैराश्यं मत्स्वरूपे निरञ्जने ॥
verses.iast: kva bhūtāni kva deho vā kvendriyāṇi kva vā manaḥ | kva śūnyaṃ kva ca nairāśyaṃ matsvarūpe nirañjane ||
verses.en: Where are the elements, where is the body, where are the senses, where is the mind, where is emptiness, where is despair, in my own spotless nature?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 20.1 is a verse from chapter 20 (Free while living). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Where are the elements, where is the body, where are the senses, where is the mind, where is emptiness, where is despair, in my own spotless nature?"

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: क्व शास्त्रं क्वात्मविज्ञानं क्व वा निर्विषयं मनः । क्व तृप्तिः क्व वितृष्णात्वं गतद्वन्द्वस्य मे सदा ॥
verses.iast: kva śāstraṃ kvātmavijñānaṃ kva vā nirviṣayaṃ manaḥ | kva tṛptiḥ kva vitṛṣṇātvaṃ gatadvandvasya me sadā ||
verses.en: Where is scripture, where is knowledge of the Self, where is a mind without objects, where is contentment, where is freedom from thirst, for me who am always beyond the opposites?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 20.2 is a verse from chapter 20 (Free while living). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Where is scripture, where is knowledge of the Self, where is a mind without objects, where is contentment, where is freedom from thirst, for me who am always beyond the opposites?"

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: क्व विद्या क्व च वाविद्या क्वाहं क्वेदं मम क्व वा । क्व बन्ध क्व च वा मोक्षः स्वरूपस्य क्व रूपिता ॥
verses.iast: kva vidyā kva ca vāvidyā kvāhaṃ kvedaṃ mama kva vā | kva bandha kva ca vā mokṣaḥ svarūpasya kva rūpitā ||
verses.en: Where is knowledge, where is not knowing, where is 'I', where is 'this', where is 'mine', where is bondage, where is freedom? How could my own nature have a form?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 20.3 is a verse from chapter 20 (Free while living). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Where is knowledge, where is not knowing, where is 'I', where is 'this', where is 'mine', where is bondage, where is freedom? How could my own nature have a form?"

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: क्व प्रारब्धानि कर्माणि जीवन्मुक्तिरपि क्व वा । क्व तद् विदेहकैवल्यं निर्विशेषस्य सर्वदा ॥
verses.iast: kva prārabdhāni karmāṇi jīvanmuktirapi kva vā | kva tad videhakaivalyaṃ nirviśeṣasya sarvadā ||
verses.en: Where are the actions already bearing fruit, where is freedom while living, where even final freedom when the body falls, for me who am always without distinctions?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 20.4 is a verse from chapter 20 (Free while living). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Where are the actions already bearing fruit, where is freedom while living, where even final freedom when the body falls, for me who am always without distinctions?"

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: क्व कर्ता क्व च वा भोक्ता निष्क्रियं स्फुरणं क्व वा । क्वापरोक्षं फलं वा क्व निःस्वभावस्य मे सदा ॥
verses.iast: kva kartā kva ca vā bhoktā niṣkriyaṃ sphuraṇaṃ kva vā | kvāparokṣaṃ phalaṃ vā kva niḥsvabhāvasya me sadā ||
verses.en: Where is the doer, where the enjoyer, where is stillness, where is stirring, where is direct knowing, where is its fruit, for me who am always without a separate nature?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 20.5 is a verse from chapter 20 (Free while living). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Where is the doer, where the enjoyer, where is stillness, where is stirring, where is direct knowing, where is its fruit, for me who am always without a separate nature?"

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: क्व लोकं क्व मुमुक्षुर्वा क्व योगी ज्ञानवान् क्व वा । क्व बद्धः क्व च वा मुक्तः स्वस्वरूपेऽहमद्वये ॥
verses.iast: kva lokaṃ kva mumukṣurvā kva yogī jñānavān kva vā | kva baddhaḥ kva ca vā muktaḥ svasvarūpe'hamadvaye ||
verses.en: Where is the world, where is the one who wants freedom, where is the yogi, where the knower, where the bound, where the free, in my own nature, which is one?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 20.6 is a verse from chapter 20 (Free while living). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Where is the world, where is the one who wants freedom, where is the yogi, where the knower, where the bound, where the free, in my own nature, which is one?"

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: क्व सृष्टिः क्व च संहारः क्व साध्यं क्व च साधनम् । क्व साधकः क्व सिद्धिर्वा स्वस्वरूपेऽहमद्वये ॥
verses.iast: kva sṛṣṭiḥ kva ca saṃhāraḥ kva sādhyaṃ kva ca sādhanam | kva sādhakaḥ kva siddhirvā svasvarūpe'hamadvaye ||
verses.en: Where is creation, where is dissolution, where is the goal, where the means, where the one who strives, where success, in my own nature, which is one?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 20.7 is a verse from chapter 20 (Free while living). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Where is creation, where is dissolution, where is the goal, where the means, where the one who strives, where success, in my own nature, which is one?"

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: क्व प्रमाता प्रमाणं वा क्व प्रमेयं क्व च प्रमा । क्व किञ्चित् क्व न किञ्चिद् वा सर्वदा विमलस्य मे ॥
verses.iast: kva pramātā pramāṇaṃ vā kva prameyaṃ kva ca pramā | kva kiñcit kva na kiñcid vā sarvadā vimalasya me ||
verses.en: Where is the knower, the means of knowing, the known, or knowing itself? Where is anything, or nothing, for me who am always spotless?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 20.8 is a verse from chapter 20 (Free while living). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Where is the knower, the means of knowing, the known, or knowing itself? Where is anything, or nothing, for me who am always spotless?"

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: क्व विक्षेपः क्व चैकाग्र्यं क्व निर्बोधः क्व मूढता । क्व हर्षः क्व विषादो वा सर्वदा निष्क्रियस्य मे ॥
verses.iast: kva vikṣepaḥ kva caikāgryaṃ kva nirbodhaḥ kva mūḍhatā | kva harṣaḥ kva viṣādo vā sarvadā niṣkriyasya me ||
verses.en: Where is distraction, where is focus, where is understanding, where is dullness, where is joy, where is sorrow, for me who am always without action?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 20.9 is a verse from chapter 20 (Free while living). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Where is distraction, where is focus, where is understanding, where is dullness, where is joy, where is sorrow, for me who am always without action?"

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: क्व चैष व्यवहारो वा क्व च सा परमार्थता । क्व सुखं क्व च वा दुखं निर्विमर्शस्य मे सदा ॥
verses.iast: kva caiṣa vyavahāro vā kva ca sā paramārthatā | kva sukhaṃ kva ca vā dukhaṃ nirvimarśasya me sadā ||
verses.en: Where is this everyday world, where is the highest truth, where is happiness, where is sorrow, for me who am always beyond deliberation?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 20.10 is a verse from chapter 20 (Free while living). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Where is this everyday world, where is the highest truth, where is happiness, where is sorrow, for me who am always beyond deliberation?"

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: क्व माया क्व च संसारः क्व प्रीतिर्विरतिः क्व वा । क्व जीवः क्व च तद्ब्रह्म सर्वदा विमलस्य मे ॥
verses.iast: kva māyā kva ca saṃsāraḥ kva prītirviratiḥ kva vā | kva jīvaḥ kva ca tadbrahma sarvadā vimalasya me ||
verses.en: Where is maya, where is the world, where is liking or disliking, where is the separate self, where is that Brahman, for me who am always spotless?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 20.11 is a verse from chapter 20 (Free while living). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Where is maya, where is the world, where is liking or disliking, where is the separate self, where is that Brahman, for me who am always spotless?"

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: क्व प्रवृत्तिर्निर्वृत्तिर्वा क्व मुक्तिः क्व च बन्धनम् । कूटस्थनिर्विभागस्य स्वस्थस्य मम सर्वदा ॥
verses.iast: kva pravṛttirnirvṛttirvā kva muktiḥ kva ca bandhanam | kūṭasthanirvibhāgasya svasthasya mama sarvadā ||
verses.en: Where is activity or rest, where is freedom or bondage, for me who am always unchanging, undivided and at home in myself?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 20.12 is a verse from chapter 20 (Free while living). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Where is activity or rest, where is freedom or bondage, for me who am always unchanging, undivided and at home in myself?"

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: क्वोपदेशः क्व वा शास्त्रं क्व शिष्यः क्व च वा गुरुः । क्व चास्ति पुरुषार्थो वा निरुपाधेः शिवस्य मे ॥
verses.iast: kvopadeśaḥ kva vā śāstraṃ kva śiṣyaḥ kva ca vā guruḥ | kva cāsti puruṣārtho vā nirupādheḥ śivasya me ||
verses.en: Where is instruction, where is scripture, where is the disciple, where is the guru, where is the goal of life, for me, the auspicious one, free of every limit?
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 20.13 is a verse from chapter 20 (Free while living). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Where is instruction, where is scripture, where is the disciple, where is the guru, where is the goal of life, for me, the auspicious one, free of every limit?"

verses.speaker: janaka
verses.sa: क्व चास्ति क्व च वा नास्ति क्वास्ति चैकं क्व च द्वयम् । बहुनात्र किमुक्तेन किञ्चिन्नोत्तिष्ठते मम ॥
verses.iast: kva cāsti kva ca vā nāsti kvāsti caikaṃ kva ca dvayam | bahunātra kimuktena kiñcinnottiṣṭhate mama ||
verses.en: Where is being, where is not-being, where is one, where is two? What more is there to say? Nothing at all rises in me.
verses.quick: Ashtavakra Gita 20.14 is a verse from chapter 20 (Free while living). King Janaka speaks it to his teacher, the sage Ashtavakra. In plain English it says: "Where is being, where is not-being, where is one, where is two? What more is there to say? Nothing at all rises in me."
